We derive the maximum single-event energy at fixed decay data, including fragment masses and charge allocation, and check capture and collection at a finite receiver in anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime. Repetitive radial extraction on successive exact stationary backgrounds uses an adaptive incident specific charge. The continuum mass-charge path identifies the switch between incident turning-point and negative-energy stopping, supported by numerical checks. The prescribed sequences terminate at nonzero residual charge before exhausting the energy reservoir, providing a protocol-dependent third-law analogy. The consumed reservoir is divided between extracted energy and irreversible growth of irreducible mass, with proportions depending on the protocol.
papers.authors: Hanjun Zou, Ruo-Cen Wu, Meng Xu, Zoujian Cao, Yun-Long Zhang

papers.title: Sharp rank thresholds and cubic support in PPT extensions of completely symmetric states
papers.abstract: For completely symmetric states on $d\ge3$ parties of actual local rank $N\ge3$, the least rank of an entangled state passing any prescribed finite positive level of the PPT extension hierarchy is $3d+N-3$. At equality, the two- and three-party marginals recover a ternary plane cubic shared by every extension. On this cubic the hierarchy becomes exact at a finite level precisely when every singularity outside the zero locus of the contraction quadratic is a split real node. We give the first exact level or an exact feasibility test for it, independent of $d$. On a smooth cubic the thresholds along the specified paths to the square of a flex tangent reduce to elliptic division and have unique rank-two Gram matrices. On reflection-invariant paths we obtain a quartic formula and the leading asymptotic constant. The least rank for entanglement itself is $3d+N-5$, and we classify equality. An explicit rational rank-nine three-qutrit state on a smooth cubic passes the first extension level and fails the second.
papers.authors: Qian Lilong, Teng Zhang

papers.title: Orbit-averaged spinning and eccentric binary black holes: Hamiltonian and integrability
papers.abstract: For over two decades, the orbit-averaged precession equations of spinning binary black holes at second post-Newtonian order have been a standard model for their spin dynamics. One of their constants of motion, the projected effective spin, underlies the stability analysis of aligned-spin configurations and the construction of analytical solutions. The system is known to be Hamiltonian and integrable, its Hamiltonian being the orbit average of the full post-Newtonian Hamiltonian. Independently, we derive this Hamiltonian from the equations of motion alone, show why the orbit average gives the correct equations, and relate its constants of motion to those of the full system. We then construct the action-angle variables and frequencies with the recently introduced method of fictitious variables, and propose a criterion for the breakdown of the integrability conditions. This criterion recovers the separatrices of simple classical systems and the up-down instability, whose thresholds we give explicitly for eccentric orbits. We also show that, when all binaries of an ensemble share the same parameters and radiation reaction does not depend on the spins, the Hamiltonian structure preserves an isotropic distribution of spin directions. We confirm numerically that isotropy can be lost when the parameters are correlated with the spin directions. Finally, we use the orbit-averaged Hamiltonian to generalize the projected effective spin to binary neutron stars, for which it is not conserved, and obtain a closed form valid for eccentric orbits.
papers.authors: Tom Colin, Sashwat Tanay, Manuel Alva-Morales, Prateek Anand

papers.title: Boundary preparation and anomalous relaxation near a black hole exceptional point
papers.abstract: We study the relaxation of a Robin scalar field near a stable exceptional point of a planar Schwarzschild AdS black hole, where finite boundary driving controls the recovery time without changing the leading decay rate at linear order. At the exceptional point, two weighted moments of the source determine the time dependence of the leading response. When the zeroth moment vanishes while the first remains nonzero, the linear time factor is eliminated, leaving an ordinary exponential decay. With suitable boundary preparation, a perturbation that retains more energy at release can nevertheless reach a common recovery threshold sooner. At the exceptional point, its recovery time advantage over a fixed reference that retains the linear factor grows as $\gamma_*^{-1}\log\log(1/\theta)$ as the common amplitude threshold $\theta$ approaches zero, where $\gamma_*$ is the common decay rate. The source moments also determine the constant term in this asymptotic time difference. Full scalar field evolution on a fixed background near the exceptional point illustrates the reversal for pulses matched in duration, boundary task, source cost, and injected work, within the time window where the small spectral splitting remains unresolved. The injected work also modifies the final spectrum through gravitational heating. When weak driving begins with a black hole at the exceptional point, the temperature rise is quadratic in the source amplitude, whereas the final pole splitting is linear in its magnitude. This splitting limits the time window over which the exceptional point recovery law can be observed.
papers.authors: Yu Shi, Sheng Long

papers.title: Neural-Network Identification of LIGO Noise Transients Using Binary Auxiliary-Channel Activity
papers.abstract: Transient noise artifacts ("glitches") in the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO), Virgo and KAGRA (LVK) detectors can mimic astrophysical signals and reduce confidence in gravitational-wave detections. The LVK's iDQ pipeline identifies these glitches by analyzing correlations between auxiliary sensors and the strain channel using the Ordered Veto List (OVL) algorithm. We revisit neural-network approaches to this problem using modern training infrastructure and introduce two architectures: GIANTS, a single network trained on all auxiliary-channel features, and TITAN, a mixture-of-experts model composed of subsystem-specific networks and a learned combiner. Evaluated on ten independent test periods spanning LIGO's third observing run, both models outperform OVL on most test sets, with TITAN providing the most consistent performance over time. We further show that nearly all predictive information contained in Omicron trigger features is captured by a simple binary indicator of auxiliary-channel activity. Networks trained on these binary inputs achieve essentially the same performance as models using the full 8,440-dimensional feature set while reducing the input dimensionality by an order of magnitude. These results demonstrate that modern neural networks provide a robust alternative to OVL and suggest that substantially simpler data representations are sufficient for accurate glitch identification in future iDQ deployments.
papers.authors: D. Chintala, J. Temple, S. Shapiro, L. Wilson, K. Wayt, M. Van Keuren, P. Neubauer, K. Rose, D. Moffa, L. Wade, M. Wade

papers.title: A Bose-Hubbard quantum thermal machine
papers.abstract: This work proposes a quantum thermal machine comprised of interacting ultracold bosons confined in a one-dimensional optical lattice and modeled by the Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian. We consider an Otto-inspired cycle with strokes that change the interaction strength between bosons, in addition to standard thermalization and compression/expansion strokes. We find that these interaction changes can be manipulated to enhance the performance of the thermal machine, outperforming non-interacting cycles. In particular, when operating as a heat engine, the cycle can achieve its largest work output and near-Carnot efficiency by compressing the medium at strong repulsion into a Mott insulator state. Additionally, we find that decreasing interactions after the compression stroke favors and enhances the engine operation, whereas increasing interactions favors refrigeration cycles. The findings of this work further show that controlling the interactions across quantum phases of matter can be harnessed as a useful thermodynamic resource.
papers.authors: Felipe Isaule, Juan E. Bernate, Francisco J. Pe\~na, Patricio Vargas, Thom\'as Fogarty

papers.title: From BBM92 Measurements to Secure Keys: Challenges in a Practical Implementation
papers.abstract: The protocol introduced by C. H. Bennett, G. Brassard and N. D. Mermin in 1992 (BBM92) is one of the most important and widely adopted quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols. As with any other QKD protocol, its practical security depends on satisfying the assumptions underlying its theoretical security proofs. Here, we examine two common implementations of BBM92: a conventional passive receiver and a time-multiplexed configuration that halves the number of detectors. We characterise the passive polarisation analysers common to both architectures and present experimental results obtained with the time-multiplexed receiver, employing a continuous-wave (CW) pumped spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) source of polarisation-entangled photon pairs and threshold detectors. We investigate the challenges encountered during post-processing when attempting to satisfy the requirements of existing security proofs and discuss the gap between theoretical security assumptions and the extraction of a provably secure cryptographic key.
papers.authors: Karolina P. Schatz, Elia Falcioni, Panagiotis Papanastasiou, Marco Lucamarini

papers.title: Bound entanglement as a trigonometric moment problem
papers.abstract: Entangled states that are positive under partial transposition (PPT) are the main obstruction to a simple description of entanglement. We study three basic questions about them within a class of multiqubit states, the mixtures, with real but possibly negative weights, of products of equatorial spin coherent states of several groups of qubits: which PPT entangled states belong to the class, how robust their entanglement is to white noise, and how small their rank can be. In this class each question becomes a question about a truncated trigonometric moment problem. Every such state is PPT across every bipartition, and it is fully separable exactly when an associated multi-level Toeplitz matrix is the moment matrix of a positive measure on the torus. We answer the three questions exactly in the following cases. For three qubits, every rank-four PPT entangled state with nonzero Lorentz invariant belongs to the class after invertible local operators, which proves a working hypothesis of Garberg, Irgens and Myrheim and yields a complete set of invariants for this seven-dimensional family; among the states with vanishing invariant, exactly a one-parameter family belongs to it. For every three-qubit state built from an unextendible product basis, the white-noise threshold for full separability is $\lambda^*=1-2/(1+\sqrt{1+s})$ with a local-unitary invariant $s\in(0,1]$, and $\lambda^*=3-2\sqrt2$ for the Shifts basis; a witness in closed form detects every entangled state of this family with eight local Pauli settings. For two groups of qubits we construct extremal states of minimal rank, and for three groups we determine the minimal rank of entanglement within the class in several configurations.
papers.authors: Lilong Qian, Teng Zhang

papers.title: Linear-mode photon counting performance and intrinsic dark current in HgCdTe APDs for quantum optical applications
papers.abstract: The performance of HgCdTe APDs for single photon detection at T=80 K has been characterized using a hybrized Resistive Trans-Impedance Amplifier (RTIA) and a deported Capacitance Trans-impedance amplifier (CTIA). The single-photon detection capacity was characterized with the HgCdTe APDs operated in linear mode with high APD gain, M>400, and hybridized with the RTIA. The measurements revealed an external photon detection efficiency (PDE) of 42 % to 55 %, and a dark count rate (DCR) of 2.6 MHz to 17 MHz, for an amplitude threshold ranging from 2.5 to 4.5 times the rms noise of the amplifier. Taking into account the unity gain quantum efficiency, QE=63%, this corresponds to an internal PDE ranging from 66 % to 86 %. Using the deported CTIA, it was demonstrated that the high level of DCR is not the intrinsic limit of the APD technology. The CTIA approach enables direct measurement of the APD dark current, Idark, with gain-normalized dark current levels as low as Idark/M=10.9 fA at M = 450. This corresponds to a DCR of 150 Hz which is compatible with the requirements for most of the quantum photonics applications.
papers.authors: Arthur Charrier (CEMHTI), Timoth{\'e}e Guerra (CEMHTI), Nicolas Baier (CEA-LETI), Julie Abergel (CEA-LETI), Antoine Coquiard (CEA-LETI), Amaury Mavel (INL - S\&N, INL - H\&N), Sebastien Renet (CEA), Frederic Berger (UR EMGR), Aur{\'e}lie Vandeneynde (CEA-LETI), Sandy Brunet-Manquat (CEA-LETI), Jean-Alain Nicolas (CEA-LETI), Jean-Luc Moro (FEMTO-ST, CNRS, UMLP), Jean-Marc Merolla (FEMTO-ST, CNRS, UMLP), Johan Rothman

papers.title: Virtual Autopurification in Translationally Invariant Quantum States
papers.abstract: We introduce virtual autopurification (VAP), a protocol for virtual purification that operates entirely within a single translationally invariant system. Virtual purification suppresses thermal fluctuations and decoherence noise by amplifying the dominant pure component of a mixed state, but its standard implementation requires multiple copies of the state and global entangled measurements. VAP avoids the multiple-copy overhead by constructing virtual copies from spatially separated subregions and performing entangled measurements only between them. Assuming clustering of correlations, we show that VAP reproduces the expectation values of the standard virtual purification protocol, with discrepancies that decay exponentially in both the buffer length and the inter-subregion distance. Numerical simulations support the theoretical predictions and demonstrate accurate implementation of virtual cooling with reduced resource requirements. Our results establish VAP as a resource-efficient and scalable approach to quantum-state purification in near-term devices.
papers.authors: Atsushi Iwaki, Hideaki Hakoshima, Nobuyuki Yoshioka

papers.title: Finite-dimensional Hopf algebras generated by the coradical
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra over a field $k$. The paper is concerned with the question of when $H$ is generated by the coradical $H_0$. We give several characterizations of this property, involving the largest Hopf ideal contained in the Jacobson radical $J(H^*)$ and the coefficient coalgebra of the injective hull of the trivial comodule. If the canonical map $H_0\to H/J(H)$ is surjective, then $H$ is generated by $H_0$ if and only if $H=H_0^3+J(H)^2$, where $H_0^3$ is the span of products of three elements of $H_0$. For finite locally free Hopf algebras of constant rank over a $k$-scheme in characteristic zero, including duals of liftings of a given Nichols algebra, the locus where this property holds is Zariski open and compatible with arbitrary base change. For a finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebra $K$ with abelian coradical over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the largest Hopf ideal contained in $J(K)$ is determined. $K^*$ is generated by its coradical if and only if $J(K)$ contains no nonzero skew-primitive elements. For liftings of quantum linear spaces and standard liftings of finite Cartan type, this condition is expressed in terms of the deformation parameters of $K$.
papers.authors: Rongchuan Xiong, Naihong Hu

papers.title: A unified approach to the time-dependent quantum harmonic oscillator via point transformations and Lie symmetries
papers.abstract: We revisit the time-dependent harmonic oscillator (TDHO) in quantum mechanics based on the notion of equivalence transformations and Lie point symmetries. Within this framework, we give the most general point transformations depending on seven parameters which map from the TDHO to the usual harmonic oscillator (HO) and the other way around. As a byproduct we reconstruct the Schr\"odinger propagator (Mehler's kernel) for the time-independent harmonic oscillator. We demonstrate, without recourse to the Lewis--Riesenwert (LR) invariant, how Lie algebraic methods enable alternative derivation of the normalized wave functions of the TDHO by constructing solutions invariant under some specific subgroup of $\SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ combined with the gauge group. We further show that, on the relevant $\SL(2,\mathbb{R})$-invariant solution family, the Lewis--Riesenfeld operator defines a compatible second-order differential constraint, thereby clarifying its relation to the Lie symmetry structure of the TDHO.
papers.authors: F. G\"ung\"or, J. Negro

papers.title: Efficient simulation of variational quantum circuits: representation, accuracy and CPU/GPU allocation
papers.abstract: Classical circuit simulation supports quantum software development and verification and provides a baseline for assessing quantum advantage. We compare gate-based statevector simulation, direct Pauli evolution and matrix product states for molecular and spin Variational Hamiltonian Ansatze and hardware-efficient ansatze on CPU/GPU systems, varying width, depth, precision and resource allocation. In the tested implementations, direct Pauli evolution benefits complex molecular VHA, whereas GPUs accelerate wider spin and hardware efficient circuits. Matrix product state is useful when limited entanglement permits accurate compression; corrected CPU FP32 can meet the tested tolerance while costing more than FP64. Workload size, startup, worker memory and task-specific profiling can change the preferred allocation. Matched NumPy Pauli updates accelerate two-layer full LiH by 3.45-fold; the GPU gives approximately 30-fold acceleration over 18-thread Aer for 28-qubit, four-layer TFIM, both in FP64. We provide a procedure for choosing representation, precision and worker allocation jointly, comparing the cost of complete energy evaluations under accuracy, memory and core constraints.
papers.authors: Vojt\v{e}ch Nov\'ak, Radovan Re\v{c}ka, Ond\v{r}ej Knebl, Ivan Zelinka

papers.title: Black hole binary mergers in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity with regularisation
papers.abstract: We study the non-linear dynamics of Chern-Simons gravity with numerical relativity for the first time. We use the regularisation prescription to obtain a well-posed initial-value formulation in the gauges commonly used in numerical relativity, and we simulate head-on collisions and binary black hole mergers in the regime of validity of effective field theory, extracting the corresponding scalar and gravitational waves. This opens up the possibility to test general effective field theories of gravity, including those with higher-than-second-order equations of motion, with gravitational waves.
papers.authors: Llibert Arest\'e Sal\'o, Maxence Corman, Pau Figueras, \'Aron D. Kov\'acs, Shunhui Yao

papers.title: On the thermal behavior of composites embedding extended general interfaces
papers.abstract: In heterogeneous materials, surface roughness, chemical incompatibility, mechanical mismatch or manufacturing defects result in imperfect bonding between the constituents. Such imperfections introduce a finite-thickness interphase zone between the constituents that possess a graded or inhomogeneous micro-structure. It is virtually impossible to resolve the behavior of such interphases. Instead, a well-established approach is to replace the interphase by a zero-thickness interface endowed with its own energetic structure. Conventional interface models define the interface temperature as an average of the temperatures of the surrounding bulk phases. However, this assumption is only adequate to represent uniform homogeneous interphases and it fails to accurately capture the behavior of graded or inhomogeneous interphases. In this work, we address this limitation by allowing for unequal contributions of the surrounding bulk phases to the interface temperature. We systematically revisit the resulting balance equations and present the computational framework for the finite element implementation of the model. We further incorporate the proposed model within the homogenization framework and derive closed-form analytical expressions for the effective thermal conductivity of fiber- and particle-reinforced composites, accouting for the influence of the extended general interface. Finally, through a series of numerical examples, we demonstrate the capabilities of the proposed model and investigate the influence of its parameters on the size-dependent thermal behavior of composites.
papers.authors: Soheil Firooz, Kashish Veda Eluri, Ali Javili, Paul Steinmann

papers.title: Long-distance continuous variable entanglement distribution over deployed fibre
papers.abstract: Continuous-variable (CV) entanglement offers deterministic generation and room-temperature coherent detection for quantum networks, but distributing it over deployed fibre has been hindered by the need to stabilise optical phase, polarisation, and timing at remote receivers. Here we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first distribution of CV entanglement over deployed metropolitan fibre using independent coherent receivers. The two modes of a two-mode squeezed vacuum state are delivered to remote nodes through 23 km ($\approx 7$ dB loss) and 450 m ($\approx 1$ dB loss) deployed fibre links. Each node uses its own free-running laser and polarisation-diverse coherent receiver. Co-propagating pilot tones enable digital recovery of timing, phase and polarisation, while inter-mode correlations fix the quadrature alignment. We certify entanglement with a Simon-Duan value of $1.915\pm 0.013$, below the separability bound of 2 and a logarithmic negativity of $0.067\pm0.011$. By replacing optical stabilisation with digital reconstruction, our approach offers a practical route towards scalable CV quantum networks.
papers.authors: Huy Q. Nguyen, Benjamin L. Larsen, Luiz C. C. P. Filho, Yijian Meng, Mikael {\O}. Lassen, Jonas S. Neergaard-Nielsen, Tobias Gehring, Ulrik L. Andersen, Adnan A. E. Hajomer

papers.title: Multiplicity criteria for the absolutely continuous spectrum of finite hopping Hermitian operators
papers.abstract: We consider locally finite-hopping Hermitian operators that admit radial-type transfer matrix sets in the sense of Sadel. We extend his spectral averaging formula from scalar spectral measures to matrix-valued spectral measures associated to a root matrix. This extension yields criteria for lower bounds on the multiplicity of absolutely continuous spectrum. As applications, we consider random decaying shell-matrix potentials on stair-like graphs with increasing-width wires and operators on the Bethe lattice. In both cases, we establish that absolutely continuous spectrum has almost surely infinite multiplicity.
papers.authors: Boris Berm\'udez-C\'ardenas, Christian Sadel, Amal Taarabt

papers.title: Cohomological Foundations of Entropic Monotonicity: The Relative Cyclic Complex, the Transgression Map, and the Entropic $c$-Theorem in $d = 2$
papers.abstract: We develop a cohomological framework for the entropic $c$-theorem in two dimensions, based on the relative cyclic complex of a pair of von Neumann algebras and on the transgression map associated with a faithful normal state. The framework identifies the positivity underlying the entropic proof as Borchers positivity of the zero-frequency component of the relative modular cocycle, which is the operator-algebraic origin of the quantum null energy condition (QNEC). The positivity results are dimension-independent: they depend only on the split property, modular $p$-nuclearity, and the half-sided modular inclusion structure. The main results of the paper are: (i) the identification of the entanglement cohomology with the kernel of the restriction map (Theorem 2.6); (ii) Borchers positivity of the relative modular cocycle (Proposition 3.8}); (iii) the finite-dimensional positivity of the entropy flux (Corollary 3.9); and (iv) the entropic $c$-theorem in $d = 2$ (Theorem 4.3), which follows from (iii) and the one-variable analysis. The $c$-theorem proof uses no ultraviolet regulator at any intermediate step. We also formulate two open problems: the cochain-level positivity of the transgression (Conjecture 3.5) and the cohomological interpretation of the QNEC (Conjecture 3.11). Both are stated as research directions, not as results of the paper; in particular, the $c$-theorem proof does not depend on either of them. The extension of the framework to the $F$-theorem in $d = 3$ and the general-$d$ program is the subject of the companion paper \cite{Rashkov:2026b}.
papers.authors: R. C. Rashkov

papers.title: Numerical integration of non-local master equations for renewal shot noise with drift and state-dependent amplitude
papers.abstract: The probability density of a system driven by a drift and a renewal train of kicks with state-dependent amplitude obeys a master equation that is non-local in space, because the kick operator $\hat{p}(i\partial_x I(x))$ is of infinite order, and, for non-exponential waiting times, non-local in time, with a memory kernel containing the propagator of the drift. Its solutions contain quasi-singular components, the never-kicked mass, which collapse onto the attractors of the drift. We present an accurate numerical method for such equations. The kick operator is a push-forward along the Marcus flow; in the Lamperti variable it becomes a translation, whose exact cell-to-cell weights follow from the cumulative distribution of the kicks, without quadrature. The drift is integrated by a conservative semi-Lagrangian step exact in time. The memory is represented by a sum of exponentials whose auxiliary fields are advected by the drift, at a cost linear in the number of steps. The never-kicked mass is transported exactly. For each ingredient we quantify the errors of simpler alternatives. The method is verified against exact solutions and event-driven Monte Carlo simulations with exact flow maps, from which it is statistically indistinguishable with $10^8$ trajectories. Parameters tuned for Gaussian kicks carry over unchanged to other kick distributions, and near a zero of the coupling, where the density vanishes faster than any power, the solution follows the known asymptotic law down to densities of order $10^{-37}$, far beyond Monte Carlo reach. As an application we compare the exact equation with its local and Poissonian approximations: in the range explored, the local equation deviates by up to 8% of the density width, also for waiting times with finite mean, consistently with an error estimate predicting larger deviations for slow drifts at long times. A Fortran implementation is available.
papers.authors: Marco Bianucci, Riccardo Mannella

papers.title: Geodesic-informed neural networks for testing spacetimes with S2
papers.abstract: Stellar orbits around Sagittarius A*, in particular that of S2, test the spacetime of the Galactic Center. Such analyses usually integrate the equations of motion for every likelihood evaluation and sample the posterior. We develop a differentiable orbit model for static, spherically symmetric spacetimes that obtains the parameters, their uncertainties and the Bayesian evidence by optimization rather than sampling. In the Geodesic-Informed Neural Network (GINN), the conserved quantities, the shape of the orbit and the redshift are computed exactly from the metric, and a neural network constrained by the geodesic equation represents the time evolution of the radial phase. The physical parameters and the network weights minimize a single loss with Adam and Gauss-Newton steps, and the curvature at the minimum gives the uncertainties and the evidence. We test this Gaussian approximation against a second-order expansion and an exact geodesic solver, and apply GINN to the S2 data in the Schwarzschild, Reissner-Nordstr\"om, hairy Horndeski, Bardeen, Janis-Newman-Winicour and Yukawa spacetimes. GINN reproduces the estimates and uncertainties of the exact solver. For Schwarzschild we find $M=(4.32\pm0.22)\times10^6\,M_\odot$ and $D=8.33\pm0.21$ kpc. No spacetime deviates significantly from Schwarzschild; a Yukawa correction, for example, is limited to $|\delta|<0.011$ (95%) at a range of about 180 AU. No additional parameter improves the fit enough to pay its Occam penalty, so the Bayes factors range from inconclusive to moderate in favor of Schwarzschild. The Gaussian approximation is accurate when the hair enters the metric linearly and conservative when it enters only through its square. When the posterior is close to Gaussian, GINN gives the estimates, their uncertainties and the evidence from a single optimization, and the same derivatives quantify departures from it.
papers.authors: Prajwal Hassan Puttasiddappa, Dennis Fremstad, Abdolali Banihashemi, David F. Mota

papers.title: Doppler effect on dual-downlink time-bin quantum key distribution and a proposed ephemeris-assisted witness-field correction
papers.abstract: Time-bin entanglement is promising for satellite Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) due to its compatibility with telecom fiber networks, but its phase-sensitive measurements are vulnerable to Doppler effects induced by satellite motion. We present a spectral-temporal framework for time-bin-entangled photon pairs generated onboard a satellite via Spontaneous Parametric Down Conversion (SPDC) and distributed to two Optical Ground Stations (OGSs) over independent downlinks with distinct Doppler shifts. Each OGS is equipped with an Unbalanced Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (UMZI) used to perform Bennett-Brassard-Mermin 1992 (BBM92) entangled-photon QKD. In a simulated Low Earth Orbit (LEO) pass with matched 400 ps analyzer delays, the received time-bin separation changes by at most 8.8 fs per link, while the combined carrier phase shifts by about 38 rad, which primarily degrades phase-basis correlations. After zero-Doppler calibration, this phase separates into independent signal-and idler-link contributions, allowing each station to correct its link Doppler phase shift locally, without real-time phase exchange between the stations. We propose an ephemeris-assisted feed-forward architecture, in which an auxiliary interferometer analyzes a co-propagating classical witness field to reconstruct the local Doppler-induced phase, which a phase modulator then compensates on the quantum channel. In a noise-free model, a 1 Hz sample-and-hold correction rate keeps the phase-basis Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER) below 2% and retains 93% of the ideal asymptotic key yield. After 18 accumulated passes, the corrected finite secret key reaches 95% of its ideal length, whereas relabeling the parity from the ephemeris without optical correction reaches only about 8%.
papers.authors: Sacha Gressani (FEMTO-ST, AUREA TECHNOLOGY, CSUG, UMLP), Luca Furfaro (FEMTO-ST, UMLP), Erik Kerstel (LAME-LIPhy, CSUG), Jean-Marc Merolla (FEMTO-ST)

papers.title: Spontaneous emission of atomic systems near metallic and semiconducting atomic chains
papers.abstract: We investigate the spontaneous emission of a quantum emitter placed near finite atomic chains described by the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. By tuning the chain from a metallic to a semiconducting character through dimerization, we analyze how the electronic structure of an atomic-scale scatterer, together with the illumination profile, determines the strength, bandwidth, and spatial structure of the spontaneous emission enhancement. The resonant enhancement depends on both spectral matching and the emitter position relative to the induced charge and field patterns. In metallic chains, the nearly harmonic energy spectrum leads to overlapping optical transitions and strong resonances. For semiconducting chains, dimerization opens a gap and leads to a modified density of electronic states, redistributing the response over a broader spectral range and reducing its peak intensity. Coulomb interactions affect the optical resonances through blueshift or modification of their spatial character, and act differently on collective and single-particle-like excitations. Finally, we show that the same mechanisms demonstrated in atomic chains persist in realistic quasi-one-dimensional systems, including trans-polyacetylene chains and graphene nanoribbons. Our findings indicate a general direction for engineering light-matter interactions at the atomic scale, and may offer design principles for tunable nanoscale photonic and quantum-optical devices.
papers.authors: Abhishek Ghosh, David Dams, Antton Babaze, Garnett Bryant, Carsten Rockstuhl, Andr\'es Ayuela, Karolina S{\l}owik, Marta Pelc

papers.title: Topological aspects of generalized Sklyanin algebras
papers.abstract: We are concerned with the topology of Casimir foliations of Sklyanin algebras and their certain generalizations. In particular, we give a complete description of the topological types and bifurcations of Casimir leaves of the original Sklyanin algebras, which improves and extends analogous results from the original papers of E. Sklyanin. Our approach is based on the so-called signature formula for the Euler characteristic of real algebraic varieties. Moreover, we show that the same approach yields similar results for certain generalizations of the original Sklyanin algebras known as Jacobian Poisson structures. Keywords: Poisson structure, Sklyanin algebra, Casimir function, Casimir foliation, Nambu bracket, Jacobian Poisson structure, Euler characteristic, algebraic formula for the Euler characteristic, bifurcation diagram, isolated singularity of complete intersection, Milnor number
papers.authors: Giorgi Khimshiashvili

papers.title: Acoustic scattering and radiation force on a global-monopole defect
papers.abstract: We investigate the scattering of scalar acoustic waves by the rigid core of a point defect described by the global-monopole geometry, \(dl^2=dr^2+\alpha^2r^2d\Omega^2\), allowing for both a deficit (\(\alpha<1\)) and an excess (\(\alpha>1\)) of solid angle. We show that this geometry can be realized exactly in a fluid with constant radial and tangential mass densities, where \(\alpha^2=\rho_t/\rho_r\). Because the metric is not asymptotically flat, a global plane wave cannot be defined, and we formulate the scattering problem in terms of partial-wave phase shifts. These separate exactly into a topological contribution, \(\frac{\pi}{2}(\ell-s_\ell)\), and a core contribution determined by spherical Bessel functions of noninteger order \(s_\ell\). We derive a closed-form expression for the topological amplitude, supplemented by an absolutely convergent remainder. The amplitude is singular on the cone \(\theta_0=\pi|1-1/\alpha|\), corresponding to the universal deflection angle of acoustic geodesics. The core amplitude obeys a generalized Rayleigh law, with a dipole exponent \(\sqrt{8+\alpha^2}/\alpha\). In the absence of translational isometries, the radiation force must be evaluated directly on the core surface. We derive a partial-wave expression for this force and show that its leading low-frequency contribution is linear in the topological phase. For every \(\alpha>1/\sqrt{6}\), except \(\alpha=1\), the force is negative within a low-frequency interval \(ka<ka_c(\alpha)\), pulling the core toward the source. For \(\alpha>\alpha_*\simeq1.372\), the normalized force diverges as \(ka\to0\).
papers.authors: \'Atila Pereira Ribeiro, Alexandre M. de M. Carvalho, Claudio Furtado

papers.title: QuFrame: Pauli Frame Tracking for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Control
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires continuous quantum error correction (QEC) to suppress physical noise. While Clifford-only workloads can defer corrections to software post-processing, universal computation breaks this paradigm: executing non-Clifford gates via magic-state gadgets introduces hard, real-time control-flow dependencies on error-corrected measurements. Consequently, the controller must extract syndromes, decode them, and update the Pauli frame in real time, closing the entire QEC loop within a strict $1\,\mu\text{s}$ cycle. However, prior proposals on Pauli frame tracking remain largely theoretical, leaving the microarchitectural bottlenecks of tracking, resolving, and synchronizing frame updates across distributed control pipelines unaddressed. To this end, we present QuFrame, a control microarchitecture for real-time Pauli frame tracking that closes the QEC loop within $1\,\mu\text{s}$ while sustaining QPU-rate throughput. By introducing QuFrameISA, we cleanly decouple instruction execution from continuous Pauli frame management. Execution is distributed across per-qubit Instruction Resolution Engines (IREs) that resolve instructions against the frame via a single table lookup, while a Pauli Frame Management Unit enables independent, lock-free concurrent commits. To strictly guarantee the $1\,\mu\text{s}$ deadline, QuFrame pairs an asynchronous primary decoder with an on-chip fallback decoder that resolves in $144\,\text{ns}$, natively reconciling divergent updates in hardware without degrading logical error rates.
papers.authors: Aleksandra \'Swierkowska, Ilgaz Er, Emmanouil Giortamis, Pramod Bhatotia

papers.title: Only the disk: topological obstructions for warped AdS$_6\times S^2$ in Type IIB
papers.abstract: Supersymmetric AdS$_6\times S^2$ solutions of Type IIB supergravity are warped products over a Riemann surface $\Sigma$. They are determined by two holomorphic differentials on $\Sigma$, with five-branes at poles on its boundary. We derive restrictions on the genus and the number of boundary components of $\Sigma$. Without seven-branes or orientifolds, the differentials are taken to be single-valued on $\Sigma$. Regularity implies that the number of interior zeros of one differential equals the total rotation of the phase of the ratio of the two differentials along the boundary. It also bounds this rotation on each boundary component by the number of poles on that component. Combined with the known count of zeros on the double of $\Sigma$, these two statements force $\Sigma$ to be a disk. With mutually local seven-branes and orientifolds as interior punctures, the same conclusion follows under additional assumptions on the global structure of the differentials and on their behavior at the punctures. The disk then admits at most one orientifold puncture. On a disk without punctures, the bound applied between successive poles also recovers the known cyclic ordering of the five-brane charges along the boundary.
papers.authors: Nakwoo Kim

papers.title: A Convex-Roof Affinity-Square Measure of Quantum Imaginarity
papers.abstract: Quantum imaginarity characterizes the part of a quantum state that cannot be represented by real density matrices in a fixed reference basis. We study an affinity-square measure of imaginarity for pure states and its convex-roof extension to mixed states. The pure state quantity is defined by minimizing the affinity-square measure over the convex set of real states. This optimization admits a closed expression determined by the modulus of the conjugation overlap between a state and its complex conjugate. The measure vanishes precisely when the state is real up to a global phase. We prove that the convex-roof extension is faithful, convex, monotone under real operations, and nonincreasing on average under selective real operations. For arbitrary single-qubit mixed states, we evaluate the convex roof exactly and express it in terms of the imaginary component of the off-diagonal density-matrix element. We also compare pure-state imaginarity with an auxiliary affinity-square coherence functional and give the corresponding phase weights.
papers.authors: Nan-Nan Guan, Meng-Li Guo, Xue-Na Zhu, Zhi-Xiang Jin, Yan-Hui Zhou

papers.title: Quantifying extractable imaginarity with qubit triangles
papers.abstract: Two qubit states with the same robustness of imaginarity can differ in the robustness attainable by real filtering on a successful outcome. We represent the input robustness $R$ and the largest conditional robustness $\kappa$ by the base of a right triangle and the slope of its hypotenuse, respectively. Twice the area, $R^2\kappa$, defines a faithful, convex measure that is monotone on average under real instruments. In arbitrary finite dimensions, maximizing the mean normalized area of the extracted qubits gives the pointwise smallest strongly monotone extension of the qubit measure. We derive computable bounds on this area by determining the maximum mean squared robustness of the output qubits. This maximum equals the Bures quantum $\chi^2$ divergence between the input and its real part. A projection onto orthogonal real subspaces attains the maximum and, when its outcome is retained, preserves the quantum Fisher information at the midpoint of a mixture of the input and its complex conjugate. We obtain exact areas for states with commuting real and imaginary parts and for pure states mixed with white noise. Two eight-dimensional states have identical $R$, $\kappa$, and optimal mean squared robustness, yet their different areas rule out deterministic conversion by real operations in one direction.
papers.authors: Meng-Li Guo, Chen-Xin Xu, Wen Xu, Shao-Ming Fei

papers.title: Lorentz and Poincar\'e holonomies of an acoustic vortex:ergoregion transition, Sagnac time, and beyond-Aharonov--Bohm phonon scattering
papers.abstract: Far from its core, a vortex in a superfluid is acoustically equivalent to a massless spinning cosmic string, and the scattering of phonons reduces to an Aharonov--Bohm (AB) problem. Beyond this limit, we compute the Lorentz and Poincar\'e holonomies in closed form, the Lorentz and Poincar\'e holonomies of the \emph{exact} acoustic geometry of an irrotational vortex for circular loops of arbitrary radius~$r$. Using the Painlev\'e--Gullstrand tetrad, which is regular inside the ergoregion, we show that the Lorentz holonomy changes conjugacy class at the ergosurface $r=\re=\Gamma/2\pi c$: it is a rotation by $2\pi\sqrt{1-\re^{2}/r^{2}}$ outside, a null rotation on, and a boost of rapidity $2\pi\sqrt{\re^{2}/r^{2}-1}$ inside. The invariant translational component of the Poincar\'e holonomy is a time shift $\tau(r)=(\Gamma/c^{2})(1-v_s^{2}/c^{2})^{-1/2}$, which we identify with half the acoustic Sagnac delay measured in the proper time of a static observer; it reduces to the spinning-string value $\Gamma/c^{2}$ as $r\to\infty$. No torsion is required: the translational holonomy follows from the Cartan development of the Levi-Civita connection. The non-topological part of the geometry leaves a long-range imprint on phonon scattering: the centrifugal term is $m^{2}+2m\alpha$ instead of the AB form $(m+\alpha)^{2}$, with $\alpha=\omega\Gamma/2\pi c^{2}$, so the $s$ wave is not phase shifted. As a consequence the transverse cross section, which controls the Iordanskii force, is $q\sigma_{\perp}=2\pi\alpha-\pi^{3}\alpha^{3}/3+O(\alpha^{5})$, rather than the AB value $\sin 2\pi\alpha$. We show that the near-zone curvature and any short-range, parity-symmetric core physics enter $\sigma_\perp$ only at $O(\alpha^{5})$, so the $\alpha^{3}$ term is universal. We give estimates for superfluid $^4$He, atomic condensates, and shallow-water analogues.
papers.authors: Claudio Furtado, A. M. de M. Carvalho, L. C. Garcia de Andrade, Fernando Moraes

papers.title: Semiclassical Quantum Mechanics and the Optics of Time-Varying Media
papers.abstract: Rapid, high contrast modulation of optical parameters such as the refractive index can radically reshape a wave's frequency spectrum as it propagates. Non-commuting frequency and time operators can be used to describe this reshaping, analogous to the position and momentum operators of quantum mechanics. Here we develop the connection between this theory and semi-classical quantum mechanics, showing that: (i) different microscopic models of time-varying materials are equivalent to choices of operator ordering; (ii) wave propagation is governed by an unusual non-Hermitian Schr\"odinger equation; (iii) we can take a semi-classical limit, finding a generalization of Hamilton's equations governing the central frequency and arrival time of a wave spectrum as it propagates through a modulated material. The theory can be applied to design dispersive time modulations that `focus' a wave in frequency and time, analogous to caustics in semiclassical quantum mechanics. Our results not only deepen the connection between classical wave propagation and quantum mechanics, but can also simplify overly complex calculations that have been previously applied to media where time reflection effects are negligible.
papers.authors: S. A. R. Horsley, R. Sokol, E. -M. Graefe

papers.title: Beyond Corpus-Driven Imitation: Evolving Musical Mindsets in the Agentic Orchestra via Quantum Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: This paper presents a framework for computer-aided music composition and performance based on quantum reinforcement learning and multi-agent interaction. We introduce the agentic orchestra, where musical agents evolve distinct mindsets through trial-and-error engagement with a musical environment, rather than through training on large datasets. The agents are implemented as parameterised quantum circuits. They evolve distinct compositional behaviours, referred to as mindsets. This enables the exploration of musical decision spaces using quantum superposition and entanglement within a hybrid quantum-classical loop. We present two complementary agent architectures: atomistic agents, which process pitch and rhythm independently, and holistic agents, which handle pitch and duration as unified note events. Mindsets are shaped through musically grounded reward functions, which can be combined and weighted to develop different mindsets across agents. The resulting system positions quantum computing agents less as autonomous composers and more as adaptive musical partners, each developing its own musical personality through interaction rather than imitation. Demonstrations show how agents generalise their learned behaviour to previously unseen material, operating in interactive and offline batch modes using MIDI-encoded music. While quantum computers are still in development, experiments conducted on IBM quantum hardware confirmed that musically meaningful learning is achievable with existing quantum computers. For composers and performers, the agentic orchestra opens new possibilities for emergent, process-oriented musical creativity, offering a scalable foundation for quantum computer-aided music composition as quantum computing technology continues to advance.
papers.authors: Eduardo Reck Miranda, Moein Fahmideh Vatandoost

papers.title: A characterization of uniformly discrete crystalline measures with unit weights
papers.abstract: We prove that every uniformly discrete set $\emptyset\ne\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ admitting a Fourier summation formula with a discrete set of frequencies $S(\Lambda)\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ arises from the Alon--Kummer--Kurasov--Vinzant construction using a Lee--Yang variety. In particular, every crystalline measure with uniformly discrete support and unit weights is a Fourier quasicrystal coming from the above construction. It also implies that every set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^d\subset\mathbb{C}^d$ as above is the common zero set in $\mathbb{C}^d$ of finitely many trigonometric polynomials, extending the one-dimensional theorem of Olevskii and Ulanovskii. As part of the proof, we generalize Meyer's notion of lighthouse measures to higher codimension and introduce lighthouse manifolds, which we characterize, up to a monomial change of coordinates, as the torus parts of Lee--Yang varieties.
papers.authors: Lior Alon, Mario Kummer

papers.title: Reconstructing the mass-redshift distribution of supermassive black holes using multiband gravitational-wave observations
papers.abstract: The formation and evolution of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) remain major open questions in astrophysics. Astrophysical models of SMBHs invoke black-hole (BH) seeds formed at high redshift, which subsequently grow through gas accretion and mergers. Although observations of high-redshift quasars and active galactic nuclei constrain these scenarios, the mechanisms governing SMBH formation and growth remain uncertain. Future gravitational-wave (GW) observations across the millihertz, decihertz, and audio-frequency bands will provide a complementary and direct probe of SMBH assembly by tracing their merger history. We investigate the extent to which multiband GW observations can reconstruct the mass-redshift distribution of these mergers. We simulate populations of BH mergers predicted by different astrophysical models and identify those observable by the millihertz detector LISA, the decihertz detector LGWA, and next-generation ground-based detectors operating in the audio-frequency band. We reconstruct the mass-redshift distribution of these mergers using the nonparametric inference code FIGARO. We find that combining observations across frequency bands substantially improves the reconstruction for the light-seed models considered here, whose merger populations span broad ranges of mass and redshift. In contrast, for the heavy-seed models considered here, LISA alone recovers most of the accessible mass-redshift distribution, with little additional improvement from the multiband network.
papers.authors: Alorika Kar, Souvik Jana, Enrico Barausse, Parameswaran Ajith

papers.title: Asymptotic analysis of a $3\times3$-doubly periodic random lozenge tiling model of a hexagon
papers.abstract: We study a random lozenge tiling model of a regular hexagon with weights that are doubly periodic with period $3$. This model features a smooth phase with six cusp points. We obtain explicit descriptions of the limit shape and the local scaling limits of the correlation kernel. Both limits are expressed as contour integrals on the Harnack curve that underlies the model, or on its double cover that is obtained by gluing together two copies along the support of an equilibrium measure in an external field. Our asymptotic analysis is based on the double contour integral representation of the correlation kernel due to Duits and Kuijlaars. This double contour integral contains a factor that is given in terms of the solution of a Riemann-Hilbert problem for matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials. The asymptotic behavior of this Riemann-Hilbert problem was recently studied by one of the authors using the Deift-Zhou method of steepest descent. In this work, we complement this approach with the asymptotic analysis of the double contour integral. The integrals are moved to the double cover of the Harnack curve. We analyze the effect of the first two transformations of the Deift-Zhou method, and deform the contours to the relevant saddle points. We visualize our asymptotic analysis on the amoeba of the Harnack curve, in the spirit of the work of Berggren and Borodin on the doubly periodic Aztec diamond.
papers.authors: Max J. van Horssen, Arno B. J. Kuijlaars

papers.title: In-memory measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution
papers.abstract: Quantum memories offer to significantly extend the performance of quantum networks, but their complexity and limited performance at telecommunication wavelengths have so far hindered practical deployment. We propose a new memory-assisted measurement device independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) protocol based on in-memory interference. Our approach leverages progress in atomic ensemble memories that enable the interference of a stationary matter qubit and a travelling photonic qubit inside a single quantum memory. We quantitatively evaluate the performance of this scheme against memoryless MDI-QKD and existing two-memory architectures, showing that it not only achieves superior secret key rates and surpasses the memoryless bound at substantially shorter distances, but also reduces hardware requirements by halving the number of memories and detectors. Our results further indicate that off resonant cascaded absorption (ORCA) memories are a particularly promising platform for implementing this protocol, and we outline a concrete design compatible with their capabilities. These findings demonstrate that in-memory interference provides a higher performance, and resource efficient route toward near term memory enhanced quantum secure communications.
papers.authors: Nicolas Gauriot, Samuel Morrissey, Paul M. Burdekin, Ilse Maillette de Buy Wenniger, Sarah E. Thomas, Ian A. Walmsley, Robert I. Woodward, R. Mark Stevenson

papers.title: Grade Restriction Rule For D-Brane Transport In Non-Abelian Gauged Linear Sigma Models
papers.abstract: We study the low energy behaviour of B-type D-branes in non-Abelian gauged linear sigma models. The main problem is to determine the grade restriction rule for D-brane transport from one phase to another along paths. We analyze the convergence condition of the integral for the hemisphere partition function. We perform a thorough analysis in a particular model with two phases, one weakly coupled and one strongly coupled, both corresponding to Calabi-Yau threefolds. General methods are developed in this study and are applied to other models successfully. The integrals for a set of special Chan-Paton representations exhibit critical behaviour around each singular point on the phase boundary. From each of these points emanate ``no entry zones'' where a convergent contour is lost or is forced to traverse Gamma function poles. Knowledge of the special representations and no entry zones is strong enough to uniquely determine the grade restriction rule. In the course of this study, we encounter a problem in Weyl invariance of convergent contours, which forces us to modify the grade restriction criterion. The special representations play an important r\^ole in the monodromy around the singular point. We also obtain exact results on boundary conditions in supersymmetric QCDs and apply them to understand the low energy behaviour of D-branes in the strong coupling phase.
papers.authors: Richard Eager, Kentaro Hori, Johanna Knapp, Mauricio Romo

papers.title: A relativistic gravitisation of quantum theory?
papers.abstract: We develop a model, that we call local semiclassical gravity, based on the distributional semiclassical Einstein field equations (EFEs) sourced by the local quantum state, i.e. the reduced density matrix of the local system updated by collapses (only) in its past light cone. We propose this as the basis of a relativistically causal generally covariant gravitisation of relativistic quantum theory in $1+3$ spacetime dimensions. We derive the weak-field limit which exhibits the explicitly causal dynamical structure of the theory, and recover the Schr\"odinger-Newton (SN) system in the nonrelativistic limit. This proposal can thus be understood as a causal completion of the SN equation, a nonlinear extension to quantum theory. We analyze relativistic quantum measurements in this nonlinear setup, showing that these do not lead to superluminal signalling if quantum states update (only) in the future light-cone of the measurement region. We give explicit examples of quantum measurements on a spatial superposition and on entangled subsystems showing how, in the weak field limit, discontinuities in the expectation value of the stress-energy tensor can be consistent with distributional solutions to the (linearised) semiclassical EFEs. We also highlight that the theory allows non-standard measurements via its nonlinearities. These effective ``readout devices'' can approximately determine a quantum state without affecting it through the state's influence on the classical gravitational field and hence can implement approximate quantum state cloning. Nonetheless, the theory does not allow superluminal signalling, although it does violate the quantum no-signalling principle. We further show that the classical gravitational field is generally not locally causal in the sense of Bell. We present several paths to test the model against low-energy quantum gravity in tabletop experiments.
papers.authors: Samuel Fedida, Adrian Kent

papers.title: Rotational Splitting of Reflectionless Matching and Virtual Absorption in a Semiopen BTZ Cavity
papers.abstract: We study complex frequency reflection zeros of a scalar field in a finite rotating BTZ region. The region is bounded by a partially reflecting near horizon wall and connected to an exterior propagation channel. We use exact radial solutions to determine the conditions for zero reflection and test their finite time behavior through wave packet evolution. Rotation splits the reflection zeros in the $m=\pm1$ sectors. For a representative pair of branches, there is a range of reflection coefficients for a passive wall in which the co-rotating incident wave must grow in time, while the counter-rotating one must decay. In the near horizon limit, the magnitude of the wall reflection coefficient mainly controls the growth or decay rate, while its phase mainly controls the oscillation frequency. Exterior matching introduces corrections to these relations. We examine four truncated wave packets, including one tuned case and three reference cases. Tuning reduces the reflected energy fraction from $(3.5$--$7.6)\times10^{-4}$ to $1.8\times10^{-4}$, with little change in wall absorption or the peak energy stored in the cavity. We also find that two co-rotating branches merge at a second-order exceptional point (EP2). A near horizon expansion determines its location and the small wall reflectivity required for its formation. Under perturbations, the reflection zeros exhibit square-root splitting, while the poles of the local-source Green's function do not merge and its response remains linear. These results distinguish scattering zeros from the intrinsic resonances of the system.
papers.authors: Sheng Long, Manman Sun, Qin Tan, Yu Shi

papers.title: Gradient Blindness in Adaptive Architecture Search for IQP Born Machines
papers.abstract: Instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) Born machines learn a probability distribution from data with a circuit of commuting gates that a classical computer trains at hundreds of qubits. Adaptive algorithms grow a sparse circuit from a small seed by adding in every round the candidate gates with the largest loss gradient. Such algorithms never add a candidate whose gradient vanishes, so the choice of seed decides which circuits they can reach. Here we show that a candidate gate has a nonzero gradient for some angles of the circuit exactly when its generator is the sum of an odd number of linearly independent generators already in the circuit. The common seed of one-qubit gates therefore never adds a gate on an even number of qubits, which exact gradients on 12 qubits confirm. A seed of one-qubit gates plus the edges of the Chow-Liu tree sees every candidate, and its circuits match the full circuits on 12 and 16 qubits with 10 to 13 percent of their parameters. At 484 qubits, a heredity pool keeps the search over higher-order gates feasible, and the circuits grown from this seed reach a lower test loss than the dense two-body circuit with 6 percent of its parameters, although the higher-order gates add no gain.
papers.authors: Sebastian W\"olckert, Gerhard Stenzel, Michael Poppel, Claudia Linnhoff-Popien, Jonas Stein

papers.title: Holomorphic Feynman diagrams in four dimensions and the quantum BPS ring
papers.abstract: We compute, at all loop orders, the kernels of the holomorphic Feynman graphs that carry the loop corrections to supersymmetry transformations and to regularized products of local operators in the holomorphic twist of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric gauge theories. The current equations of these holomorphic graph integrals are those of an electrical network. Schwinger parameters are resistances and holomorphic momenta are injected currents. Iterating series, parallel and star--triangle reductions on Schwinger space gives the fan, spider and cubic product-forest kernels at all loop orders. Assuming that twisting commutes with quantization for these composite operators, we identify the twisted differential with their loop-corrected supersymmetry transformation. We give every perturbative correction to the supersymmetry transformation in $\mathcal N=4$ Yang--Mills theory, including its action on operators with arbitrary holomorphic derivatives. Using the marked higher operations of Gaiotto, Kulp and Wu, we also construct and compute the quantum product of operators and prove that, on $\mathbf Q$-cohomology, it is associative, graded commutative and unital, supplying the multiplication of the quantum BPS ring. Every multi-graviton operator thus has an explicit finite completion to a cocycle of the full quantum supercharge. Our computer census finds new fortuitous classes and one-loop lifts in $\mathcal N=4$ Yang--Mills theory with several gauge groups. We have found no two-loop lift in the sectors tested. We also find two-loop lifts in the Leigh--Strassler and $\beta$-deformations of $\mathcal N=4$ Yang--Mills theory. In other theories, we find two-, three- and four-loop lifts in abelian gauge theories, and two- and three-loop lifts in $\mathcal N=2$ $SU(2)$ and $SU(3)$ gauge theories and their singlet deformations.
papers.authors: Botao Li, Kangning Liu, Chi-Ming Chang

papers.title: Quantum Parallel Algorithm for Multivariate Trace Estimation with Applications
papers.abstract: Estimating multivariate traces Tr(A1A2......Ak) is a fundamental task arising across diverse fields. In this paper, We develop a quantum algorithm for this problem tailored to near-term quantum devices. We access matrices by preparing their vectorized states. This access mode yields a tensor-network representation of the multivariate trace, which in turn guides the design of a parallel algorithm. The resulting circuit has depth dominated solely by that of the input oracle and independent of the number of matrices k, at the cost of a qubit count scaling as {\Theta}(k)-a trade-off between circuit depth and circuit size. Moreover, the circuit exhibits a simple modular structure that allows explicit distribution over O(k) devices. We further establish efficient preparation circuits for a broad range of matrix classes, demonstrating the wide applicability of our approach. we present two applications: spectral sum estimation and a quantum implementation of the classical Lanczos method. Both reduce the target problem to sums of multivariate traces, thereby avoiding the construction of matrix polynomial transformations and achieving two levels of parallelism. For certain matrix classes, the resulting algorithms reduce circuit depth by a factor equal to the degree of the approximating polynomial. The shallow circuit depth and distributed implementation make our algorithms particularly suitable for near-term devices.
papers.authors: Honghong Lin, Yun Shang

papers.title: Canonical weight-two algebras and strongly generated vertex operator superalgebras
papers.abstract: This paper studies vertex operator superalgebras strongly generated by their weight-1, weight-$\frac{3}{2}$ and weight-2 homogeneous subspaces. The presence of a nontrivial weight-1 subspace introduces derivative and quadratic current terms in weight-2. To address this, we use low-weight quasi-primary projections to identify two canonical commutative associative algebras, $\mathcal{A}$ and $A$, within the weight-2 subspace. We demonstrate that the algebraic structures of the generating subspaces are encoded by a quadruple that generalizes Lie--Rinehart algebras and their weak representations. This quadruple yields necessary and sufficient compatibility conditions for constructing an associated Lie superalgebra $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{g},A,U)$. Based on this, we construct a family of universal vertex operator superalgebras $V_{\mathcal{L}}(\ell,0)$ and establish a reconstruction theorem for their simple quotients under certain conditions. If $A$ is finite-dimensional, we prove that its orthogonal idempotent decomposition into local Artinian summands naturally induces a tensor product isomorphism of the corresponding vertex operator superalgebras. In addition, our general construction encompasses many vertex operator superalgebras, such as superconformal algebras and generalized $\mathrm{BMS}_3$ (super)algebras.
papers.authors: Jinrong Wang, Xiaoqing Yue

papers.title: Gauge and scale dependence of the quadratic backreaction source during inflation: Uniform-expansion gauge
papers.abstract: Cosmological backreaction is most directly expressed through the local expansion of the spacetime foliation, so uniform-expansion (UE) slicing provides a natural geometrical setting in which to examine the quadratic effective energy-momentum tensor (2EMT) of scalar perturbations during slow-roll inflation. We impose the complete scalar gauge conditions $\kappa=0$ and $E=0$. The uniform-expansion condition gives a \textit{differential} constraint for the shift $Q$ in configuration space and satisfies $Q_{\mathrm{UE}}(k)=-3(\Psi'+\mathcal H\Psi)/(k^2+3\epsilon\mathcal H^2)$ for each Fourier mode. In the strict infrared, the UE source vanishes at zero gradient, while its first nonzero terms are $\widehat\tau_{00}^{\mathrm{UE}}/\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LW}} \simeq8\sigma_1^2/\epsilon$ and $\widehat\tau_{ii}^{\mathrm{UE}}/\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LW}} \simeq-8\sigma_1^2/(3\epsilon)$ at leading slow-roll order. Thus $w_{\rm raw}^{\mathrm{UE}}\simeq-1/3$, but the first finite-gradient coefficients differ from the comoving and uniform-density gauges. Sufficiently deep in the gradient-dominated intermediate infrared, the leading UE behavior approaches the spatially-flat result, whereas the crossover region between the strict and intermediate infrared regimes requires the full expressions for the 2EMT. In the ultraviolet, we have $\widehat\tau_{00}^{\mathrm{UE}}\simeq2\mathcal F_{\mathrm{SW}}$ and $\widehat\tau_{ii}^{\mathrm{UE}}\simeq(2/3)\mathcal F_{\mathrm{SW}}$, yielding $w_{\mathrm{raw}}\simeq1/3$. Separately, we demonstrate the gauge dependence of the 2EMT under general scalar gauge transformations and discuss the complete fixing of the UE gauge.
papers.authors: Inyong Cho

papers.title: Stabilizer models of achiral abelian topological orders
papers.abstract: We construct continuous-variable stabilizer codes realizing every achiral 2D abelian topological order, both bosonic and fermionic. Starting from an arbitrary signature-zero integer $K$-matrix, we show that the corresponding topological order can be obtained by condensing a lattice of dyons with trivial pairwise mutual braiding in an $\mathbb{R}^N$ gauge theory. We implement this condensation microscopically by gauging a non-on-site 1-form symmetry of the $\mathbb{R}^N$ toric code.
papers.authors: Marvin Qi, Wilbur Shirley

papers.title: Quantum Annealing with a Quantum Neural Network: Width of Annealing Matters
papers.abstract: Quantum annealing is a promising quantum algorithm for dealing with computationally hard optimization problems. Currently available hardware can implement the algorithm for a significant class of Hamiltonian problems. However, its performance is especially limited in discontinuous quantum phase transitions, where the energy gap shrinks exponentially with system size. In this paper, we introduce an extension of quantum annealing to a quantum neural network and study its performance in a number of prototypical optimization problems. In particular, we observe that already a random quantum annealing network of width W = 2 can exponentially reduce the number of evolution layers or depth of the annealing process in the quantum search problem. By tuning the network parameters the search problem can be solved with exponentially small errors by a quantum perceptron of depth L = 1 and width W = 2. The findings show that width of a quantum annealing network is critical to enhance the success probability of the algorithm by providing a larger and learnable evolution space for the annealing process.
papers.authors: Mojtaba Asadollahi, Danial Khajehzadeh, Abolfazl Ramezanpour

papers.title: CCZ gate beyond the strong Rydberg-blockade regime
papers.abstract: We present a protocol for implementing a controlled-controlled-Z (CCZ) gate on a neutral-atom platform, employing three individually addressable atoms confined in a linear array of optical tweezers and operating under finite Rydberg-Rydberg interaction (RRI). The protocol combines successive excitation of the Rydberg atoms with analytically determined pulses and uses two Rydberg levels to access opposite-sign interaction shifts. We show two different paths to get the conditional phase in the target atom: a pair of target pulses with opposite phases and a single detuned target pulse followed by a local phase correction. We derive analytical expressions for the time-integrated Rydberg populations to calculate the associated decay errors and also evaluate gate performance through master-equation simulations. Numerical comparisons with a fast Rydberg-antiblockade (RAB)-based CCZ protocol show improved gate performance at larger interatomic separations within the parameter regime considered. Monte Carlo sampling further quantifies the sensitivity to thermally induced position fluctuations. These results identify the tradeoffs between gate duration, Rydberg-state exposure, and interaction sensitivity, providing an analytically specified route to native three-qubit phase gates beyond the strong-blockade regime.
papers.authors: Snigdhadev Ray, Sinchan Snigdha Rej

papers.title: Long lived QNM for multiple black holes
papers.abstract: We provide a rigorous definition of quasinormal modes (QNM) for the Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetimes with multiple extremal black holes. For certain configurations, the trapped set of the null geodesic flow contains stable (elliptic) orbits. We analyze this phenomenon in the case of two black holes of equal mass and show that it produces QNM converging exponentially fast to the real axis. QNM for black holes have been extensively studied for $\textit{single}$ black holes and this appears to be the first $\textit{mathematical}$ result for the case of multiple black holes.
papers.authors: Ning Tang, Zhongkai Tao

papers.title: Reliability of quantum communication over erasure channels
papers.abstract: Quantum information can be reliably transmitted at rates below the quantum capacity with an error that vanishes as the number of channel uses grows. The reliability function characterizes the optimal exponential decay rate of this error. For quantum erasure channels with a prime input dimension, we determine the reliability function exactly at all positive communication rates below capacity that meet or exceed an explicit critical rate. Notably, stabilizer coding strategies attain this optimal reliability throughout this regime.
papers.authors: Hongyu Mao, Kun Fang

papers.title: Odd-Even Effects on Liouvillian Spectra and Relaxation Dynamics in Boundary-Driven Spin Chains
papers.abstract: We investigate odd-even effects on Liouvillian spectra and relaxation dynamics in boundary-driven XY and cluster chains. With the bulk couplings and boundary dissipation rule fixed, the parity of chain length determines whether non-decaying oscillatory modes exist. Consequently, odd- and even-sized chains exhibit qualitatively different dynamical behaviors. We trace this mechanism to the coupling between bulk Majorana paths and the boundary jump operators. An isolated path supports undamped modes, and products of an even number of its Majorana operators span a non?decaying subspace of even operators. This structure yields nonzero purely imaginary eigenvalues of the Liouvillian and persistent contributions to bond correlations or magnetization after preparation in product states. The mechanism extends to cluster interactions of even range under a fixed boundary dissipation rule. The existence and frequencies of the persistent modes are independent of the magnitudes of the positive boundary dissipation rates. Our results unveil how chain parity controls the existence of persistent dynamics.
papers.authors: Zhen-Yu Zheng, Shu Chen

papers.title: Accelerating Quantum Error Correction Simulations under Coherent Noise with Compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product States
papers.abstract: Reliable assessment of quantum error correction requires understanding how coherent errors affect logical performance. Although tensor networks naturally capture coherent interference, entanglement growth and large qubit counts make repeated sampling costly. Here we develop a compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product State (CAMPS) framework that reuses Clifford transformations across shots, recycles qubits released by measurements, evolves a compressed residual state, and accelerates sampling through rotation fusion and compilation tailored to the MPS layout. Surface-code benchmarks under fixed-sign coherent noise yield accurate logical error estimates at small bond dimensions, while random-sign simulations up to distance $d=9$ and on the $[[72,12,6]]$ bivariate bicycle code match the Pauli-twirling approximation results. Compared with uncompiled CAMPS, compiled CAMPS converges at smaller bond dimensions and achieves order-of-magnitude sampling speedups at equal bond dimension, opening a scalable route to studying coherent error propagation in larger fault-tolerant circuits.
papers.authors: Jiale Huang, Yaojian Chen, Ke Liu, Dingshun Lv, Mingpu Qin

papers.title: Vanilla Adiabatic Quantum Optimization Can Have Subexponential Advantage
papers.abstract: We construct a family of objective functions $f \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ for which vanilla adiabatic quantum optimization along $H(s) = -(1-s)\sum_{i=1}^n X_i + s\sum_x f(x)\lvert x\rangle\!\langle x\rvert$ finds the global minimizer in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time, whereas any classical algorithm requires $\exp(n^{\Omega(1)})$ time to do so in the black-box model. Our result is achieved by replacing the linearization technique in an earlier work of Leng et al. (arXiv:2504.14841), which establishes a similar subexponential quantum speedup using a transverse field Ising mixer rather than $-\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$.
papers.authors: Yufan Zheng

papers.title: Distinguishing Conserved Quantum Sectors via Measurement Record Features
papers.abstract: Conservation laws partition the Hilbert space of a quantum system into invariant sectors that are often difficult to identify directly. Repeated measurements on an ancillary probe, however, generate a measurement record that provides information about the occupied sector. Here we develop a framework for identifying conserved sectors using a $(K+1)$-dimensional feature vector of record statistics, comprising the average outcome frequency and pair-outcome correlations up to $K$ measurement cycles apart. For fixed $K$, the feature vector can be evaluated at a cost linear in record length. In quantum non-demolition measurement models, the average outcome frequency suffices for accurate sector identification. For an interacting spin bath with nontrivial dynamics within each sector, incorporating temporal correlations between successive and more widely separated measurements into the record feature vector substantially improves classification fidelity. Our framework provides an efficient approach to conserved-sector identification and demonstrates the importance of temporal correlations in distinguishing the underlying sector dynamics.
papers.authors: Hao Zhu, Guo-Feng Zhang, Wen-Long Ma

papers.title: Topological Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: Scaling universal quantum computation and implementing quantum machine learning with protected logical qubits remain challenging. To harness the computational potential of existing fault-tolerant quantum platforms, we introduce topological quantum reservoir computing, a novel approach using protected degrees of freedom for storage and the host system's intrinsic dynamics for information processing. Using a one-dimensional Kitaev chain, we show how long-lived Majorana edge modes and fast bulk responses support these complementary functions within the same many-body system. We identify the tradeoffs governing access to protected memory and show how matched interfaces enable programmable writing and interactions enable autonomous information consolidation from the bulk to the edge. These mechanisms improve performance on tasks requiring long-term retention of temporal information. Our results establish topology as a new resource for quantum reservoir computing and open a route toward near-term quantum computing and quantum machine learning.
papers.authors: Zhi-Lei Zhang, Lianxiang Cui, C. P. Sun, Kohei Nakajima, Kazuyuki Aihara

papers.title: A Lie-Group Approach to Alfv\'enic Turbulence: The SO(3) Rotational p-model
papers.abstract: The inner heliosphere is permeated by fully developed, highly intermittent nonlinear turbulence. Conventional stochastic models synthesize these multiscale fluctuations by injecting additive noise within a flat Euclidean space. However, such approaches fundamentally violate the topological constraints of ideal magnetohydrodynamics, inadvertently breaking the kinetic incompressibility of the plasma and introducing spurious magnetic compressibility. To preserve the exact geometrical invariants of Alfv\'enic fluctuations, a novel mathematical framework is presented: the rotational p-model. By mapping a multifractal singular measure directly into the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ and integrating the associated stochastic differential equations in the Stratonovich sense on the spherical manifold $S^{2}$, the model generates highly intermittent, scale-dependent rotational dynamics. This Lie-group formulation conserves the magnetic field modulus while perfectly reproducing the fractional spectral envelopes and the non-Gaussian directional intermittency observed in space plasmas. Furthermore, by isolating purely directional reorientations, the framework provides exact analytical control over the waiting time statistics of magnetic intermittent bursts and the multifractal scaling exponents of angular deflections, offering a powerful new paradigm for the study of nonlinear turbulent phenomena.
papers.authors: Daniele Telloni, Sabrina Guastavino, Gary P. Zank, Luca Sorriso-Valvo, Michele Piana

papers.title: Topological Origin of Directional Amplification in Arbitrary-Dimensional Non-Hermitian Lattices
papers.abstract: In non-Hermitian lattices, combinations of gain, loss and nonreciprocal couplings can generate exponentially growing directional amplification with applications in signal processing and precision measurement. An intriguing question is whether such amplification has a universal topological origin in arbitrary dimensions. Here we establish a dimension-independent framework to uncover the topological origin of directional amplification based on the concept of amoeba, which is the logarithmic image of the singularities of the response generating function.
