The flux sectors are the 't$~$Hooft sectors of the 5d 1-form symmetries. On the tensor fluxes, the 6d Green--Schwarz couplings fix the weights, whose fractional exponents we read as the mixed anomalies of the 6d 2-form symmetry with the KK $\mathrm{U}(1)$, gravity, flavour and $\mathrm{SU}(2)_R$. The fluxes forced in each sector decide between a 2-group and a mixed anomaly. For instance, the twisted frames $\mathfrak{su}(4)_{0,4}+4\Lambda^2$ carry a non-split $\mathbb{Z}_4$ 2-group, while, in $\mathfrak{su}(4)_2+4\Lambda^2$ and $\mathfrak{su}(4)_6+2\Lambda^2$, the instanton symmetry is locked to the flavour centre and only a mixed anomaly remains. The same method applies to the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ gauging of two, three and four copies of the $E_1$ theory, which describes, respectively, $\mathrm{SU}(4)_0$, pure $\mathrm{Spin}(8)$ and the untwisted $\mathfrak{so}(8)$ KK theory. There, the fluxes exhibit the extensions of 1-form symmetries inherited from the $E_1$ 2-groups, identify the states that break each accidental 1-form symmetry and the background to which it is locked, and give the 5d 2-group to which the $S_3$-invariant 6d 3-group reduces.
papers.authors: William Harding, Noppadol Mekareeya

papers.title: Quadratic Sum Rules for Scalar Amplitudes
papers.abstract: Kleiss--Kuijf and Bern--Carrasco--Johansson relations, and their string monodromy generalizations, have long provided some of the most powerful and useful constraints on partial amplitudes. Motivated by their success, we uncover a new class of quadratic-sum rules that connect scalar amplitudes at different multiplicities. Combining recursion, kinematic shifts, and symbolic regression, we establish them for the nonlinear sigma model and its string-inspired extensions. We then extend these relations to diagonal elements of the inverse Kawai--Lewellen--Tye matrix and subsequently to planar scalar theories with nonderivative interactions and general propagators.
papers.authors: Karol Kampf, Ji\v{r}\'i Novotn\'y, David Podiv\'in, Jonah Stalknecht

papers.title: Quantum Cooling by Classical Shadows
papers.abstract: Cooling to ground states of many-body Hamiltonians by imaginary-time evolution is central to quantum simulation, but its non-unitary aspect prevents direct implementation on a quantum computer. Existing routes restore it by importing structure from outside the intrinsic quantum dynamics, e.g. by parameter estimation on many copies or recursive compilation. Here, we show that a single randomized snapshot of the quantum many-body system is sufficient to steer the state along the cooling direction on average. Our algorithm, shadow chain, uses randomized measurements to collapse the state to its classical record, which fixes the next unitary update. Snapshots across steps form a trajectory that is a quantum-executable sample of an auxiliary-field path integral; fluctuations among trajectories are exponentially suppressed in system size. With the randomness supplied intrinsically by the Born measurement rule, the trajectories sample themselves rather than going through external accept-reject steps. The resulting algorithm is ansatz-free and exact upon extrapolation to the continuous limit, with the exponential cost confined only to system size rather than temperature.
papers.authors: Xuepeng Wang, Debanjan Chowdhury

papers.title: Black Hole Superradiance and the Gravitational Auger Effect
papers.abstract: Black hole superradiance is a powerful probe of nature's light degrees of freedom. In the vicinity of a spinning black hole, it exponentially amplifies ultralight bosons from vacuum fluctuations to a macroscopic cloud of enormous occupation number. Observational superradiance effects - modified black-hole spins, gravitational-wave and coherent boson emission - are known to depend sensitively on bosonic self-interactions as induced by a quartic, $\lambda \phi^4$. Here we point out that purely gravitational interactions within the cloud significantly modify superradiance dynamics, through an analog of the Auger effect. Moreover, we identify nontrivial evolution of the superradiant levels beyond the first, driven by scattering into even higher levels and their radial overtones. For the QCD axion, the irreducible gravitational coupling rapidly dissipates the first superradiant level after it reaches saturation, through scalar emission and absorption by the black hole, while truncating the growth of higher levels. This can dramatically suppress the observability of continuous gravitational-wave signals or signatures in late binary inspirals. Black hole spin-down remains more robust, but for higher modes begins earlier and proceeds more slowly, requiring revision of existing limits.
papers.authors: Joshua W. Foster, Nicholas L. Rodd

papers.title: Constants and Nonperturbative Corrections in $V^{5,2}$ Theories
papers.abstract: We study perturbative and exponentially small corrections to the on-shell effective twisted superpotentials of two three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theories associated with free and fixed-locus cyclic quotients of the non-toric Sasaki-Einstein manifold $V^{5,2}$. These are the two-node Chern-Simons theory at levels $(k,-k)$ and the one-node flavored theory with $N_f$ fundamental pairs, respectively. At superconformal chemical potentials, we propose the Chern-Simons counterpart of the all-order perturbative expression for the flavored theory and obtain convergent integral representations for the rank-independent constants of both theories. At integer parameters, these constants admit explicit evaluations involving finite sums of Clausen functions and $\zeta(3)$, while their large-parameter expansions Borel sum to the defining integrals. At $k=1,3$ and $N_f=1,3$, we conjecture complete exponential remainders expressed through Eichler integrals of weight-four Eisenstein series. Supported by high-precision Bethe solutions, the resulting completions coincide at unit quotient order but differ at order three. We determine the minimal modular levels of the Eisenstein generators and establish convergence and natural boundaries for their primitives. Within the relative M-theory localization prescription, a complementary bulk analysis recovers the Chern-Simons shifted rank and constant in the $b\to0^+$ limit of the squashed-sphere partition function. We propose a generalization incorporating fixed-locus contributions that yields the corresponding flavored-theory result. The two theories therefore share a modular structure in their nonperturbative coefficient laws, but distinct perturbative shifts and exponential corrections resolve differences invisible in their common leading $N^{3/2}$ behavior.
papers.authors: Seyed Morteza Hosseini

papers.title: Rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising models from a tetrality web
papers.abstract: We construct rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising (TIM) models by using different chiral symmetries to prepare their folded boundary states. We use a moving up procedure which extends the product theory to an auxiliary coset with an $S_3$ automorphism group, where permutations give twisted Cardy states. We complement this with a moving down approach which reduces to the $S_3$ invariant algebra. Overall, these procedures uncover a tetrality web relating four different theories. Pulling back ordinary Cardy states of the smallest theory in the web to the physical tensor product system gives eighteen factorized interfaces and six transmitting interfaces. The latter agree with four transposition and two 3-cycle twisted boundaries in the largest theory. They include Gaiotto's RG wall and the interface obtained by fusing an Ising duality line into it. The six interfaces carry the regular action of the TIM fusion ring and have the same energy transmission coefficient, $35/48$. Their boundary entropies, bulk correlations and operator spectra distinguish them. We calculate these observables and the complete annulus amplitudes between the twenty four boundaries.
papers.authors: Ant\'onio Antunes, Jin Chen, Junchen Rong

papers.title: Optimal Frobenius light cones for power-law systems in any dimension
papers.abstract: We prove optimal Frobenius Lieb-Robinson bounds for power-law systems with power-law exponent $\alpha$ in any dimension $d$, in particular showing that the algebraic to linear light cone transition occurs at $\alpha=d+1$. The proof uses a spectral clipping method and concentration result to allow for running a multiscale operator-norm argument which produces the optimal Frobenius norm exponent. Additionally, we prove there is a Frobenius light cone transition from polylogarithmic to algebraic at the summability threshold $\alpha=d$, and a transition from decaying in volume to non-decaying in volume at $\alpha=d/2$.
papers.authors: Laura Shou, An Le, Twesh Upadhyaya, T. C. Mooney, Alexey V. Gorshkov

papers.title: Gravitational Memory Correlators and BMS Symmetry
papers.abstract: We compute the n-point memory and mixed energy-memory correlators for scalar decay into gravitons using the in-in formalism at leading order in perturbative quantum gravity. We obtain compact results for arbitrary n and explicitly verify the supertranslation flux balance relation between memory, energy, and Bondi mass detectors, realizing asymptotic symmetry constraints on infrared-finite observables.
papers.authors: Enrico Herrmann, Ian Moult, Brett Oertel, Julio Parra-Martinez, Biswajit Sahoo

papers.title: Schwarzschild scattering from CFT
papers.abstract: We show that retarded CFT correlators on $\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{S}^2$ in a state described by the small black hole in AdS$_4$ can be used to derive asymptotically flat Schwarzschild partial-wave S-matrix elements, including its spectrum of quasinormal modes. This is achieved by identifying a class of operators for which the dual bulk fields behave as plane waves near the AdS boundary for sufficiently high frequencies. For such operators there is a simple analytic relation between CFT correlators and reflection coefficients which behaves gracefully in the flat space limit, $L\to \infty$. These include spin-1, spin-2, and conformally coupled scalars. We provide a simple toy model that captures how dissipative QNMs can appear for short times inside Hermitian systems, closely resembling the small black hole in AdS.
papers.authors: Paolo Arnaudo, Benjamin Withers

papers.title: A treatment of d-dimensional Coulomb-Sturmians with noninteger quantum numbers and their connection to the radial momentum operator
papers.abstract: The Bagci-Hoggan exponential-type orbitals, the generalization of Coulomb-Sturmians to noninteger quantum numbers, were recently identified as d-dimensional Coulomb-Sturmians. In the present study, this identification is treated in detail. The radial differential equation for these orbitals is derived directly from their closed form. It represents the general Coulomb-Sturmian differential equation for quantum numbers with real values. The solution is verified through a power series representation and a first-order matrix form based on the Green's function of the radial Laplacian. New transformation relationships between these orbitals and Slater-type orbitals with noninteger principal quantum numbers are established. The radial differential equation is expressed in terms of the radial momentum operator. The expectation values of the position and radial momentum operators are obtained in closed form. The radial and Heisenberg uncertainty products, the Shannon entropy and the Fisher information are derived in general form.
papers.authors: Ali Ba\u{g}c{\i}, Z\"uhra G\"une\c{s}

papers.title: Observables and Symmetries in Causal Fermion System
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay of observables and symmetries in the framework of causal fermion systems (CFS). We show that position observables transform covariantly under unitary symmetries and for static CFS we derive their Heisenberg-type evolution. To give these results a geometric interpretation, we establish conditions under which spacetime isometries induce symmetries of CFS constructed from solutions of the Dirac equation. The crucial link is provided by the Dirac equation itself, which relates the infinitesimal generators of the geometric and CFS symmetries. In static spacetimes, this allows us to identify the generator of the induced unitary symmetry with the spatial Dirac Hamiltonian.
papers.authors: Patrick Fischer, Claudio F. Paganini, Sahil Yadav

papers.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
papers.abstract: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about \(8\%\).
papers.authors: Jing Zhou, Ligong Bian

papers.title: Relativistic and quantum fluid dynamics: nonlinear momentum evolution
papers.abstract: We present an alternative framework for nonlinear momentum evolution in fluid dynamics, in which relativistic effects are proposed as an underlying mechanism for nonlinear behavior, even in the low-velocity regime. By interpreting the second-order velocity diffusion equation from a quantum-mechanical perspective, we establish a connection between higher-order viscous transport and the reduced Planck constant, identifying the second-order viscosity coefficient with \(\hbar\). Furthermore, we show that the coupling of second-order velocity diffusion and nonlinear momentum evolution leads to a Dirac-type equation for quantum fluids. These findings reveal a potential connection among relativistic effects, higher-order fluid transport, and quantum wave dynamics.
papers.authors: Fei Wang

papers.title: Quantum Transitions From Integrable to Chaotic
papers.abstract: The quantum integrable-to-chaotic transition is commonly pictured as the quantum counterpart of the classical Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) scenario: a phaseout transition in which a family of regular eigenstates coexists with, and gradually yields to, chaotic eigenstates. Here we show that this is not the only fundamental route from integrability to chaos in quantum systems. We identify a second elementary transition---the morphing transition---which has no classical counterpart: all eigenstates hybridize and turn chaotic concurrently, so that no regular subsequence survives at any stage of the crossover. The two transitions are spectrally distinct: the phaseout spectrum is an independent superposition of regular and chaotic subsequences with Berry-Robnik statistics and a finite short-spacing intercept $P(0)$, whereas the morphing spectrum exhibits global level repulsion with Lenz-Haake statistics and $P(0)=0$. We demonstrate both transitions, and their mixture, in three models. The results for the deformed boson model further show that the quantum phaseout scenario is conditional on a smooth quantum-classical correspondence.
papers.authors: Sizhe Yan, Biao Wu

papers.title: Quantum-inspired orthogonal adapters for certifiably robust medical image classification
papers.abstract: Medical image classifiers require not only high accuracy but also reliable predictions under small input perturbations. Certified robustness provides mathematical guarantees of prediction stability, but preserving these guarantees when adapting pretrained models to new tasks remains challenging. We propose a fine-tuning approach based on quantum-inspired orthogonal butterfly layers that preserves the Lipschitz bounds of pretrained certified networks. Inspired by quantum circuits of reconfigurable beam splitters, these layers preserve orthogonality by construction using only $\mathcal{O}(n\log n)$ trainable parameters. Their structured design enables efficient classical implementation and offers a path toward future quantum implementations with logarithmic circuit depth under suitable connectivity assumptions. Controlled experiments on MNIST and MedMNIST demonstrate improved certified robustness compared with conventional alternatives and, in the DermaMNIST transfer, greater resistance to the tested attacks than low-rank adaptation (LoRA). We then apply it to trichoscopic image classification for alopecia diagnosis and alopecia areata activity assessment. By adapting a certified ImageNet-pretrained network, butterfly fine-tuning achieves approximately twice the certified accuracy of conventional fine-tuning and LoRA, with comparable classification accuracy on the same backbone and data split and similar empirical resistance to the tested adversarial attacks. Larger robustness guarantees, including certificates covering certain image-processing transformations, can be obtained at the cost of reduced accuracy. These results highlight the potential of quantum-inspired butterfly layers for parameter-efficient adaptation of medical image classifiers while preserving the mathematical guarantees underlying certified robustness.
papers.authors: Olga Tsurkan, Laia Domingo, Victoria Orlova, Asel Sagingalieva, Iris Zalaudek, Raffaele Dante Caposiena Caro

papers.title: Field algebras associated with non-symmetric lattices
papers.abstract: Field algebras, introduced by Bakalov and Kac, generalize vertex algebras by replacing locality with a weaker associativity-type axiom. We develop the structure theory of field algebras with a view toward geometric examples in which a natural bilinear form fails to be symmetric. We prove a reconstruction theorem for field algebras, producing a field algebra structure from a generating family of fields. We associate to every finite-rank lattice $L$ equipped with an arbitrary bilinear form a canonical field algebra $V_L$, generalizing the Heisenberg and lattice vertex algebras. We then study potential definitions of commutants in this setting and analyze when they are realized as subfield algebras. Finally, we realize these constructions geometrically by looking at the homology of the moduli stack of complexes of quiver representations, extending previous results from Dominic Joyce.
papers.authors: Mohamed Wacyl Meddour

papers.title: Directional gate-error asymmetry and universal selectivity bounds in non-unital open quantum systems
papers.abstract: Clifford randomized benchmarking and average gate fidelity assign a single trajectory-independent decay rate to a noisy quantum gate at leading order in the dimensionless damping exposure \varepsilon = \gamma T, concealing state-dependent transition-error asymmetries in untwirled quantum circuits. While state-dependent amplitude-damping errors are well known in open quantum systems, a trajectory-level analytical framework that bounds directional transition selectivity across arbitrary pulse shapes and Markovian environments has been lacking. Using first-order toggling-frame perturbation theory for a two-level qubit coupled to a Markovian bath, we show that the antipodal survival-error slopes \chi_+ and \chi_- along any piecewise-continuous control path depend exclusively on its time-averaged Bloch vector m and transverse residence covariance matrix G, obeying the complete-positivity cofactor bound \beta(r) \le 1. On a standard polar \sqrt{X} gate, longitudinal T_1 relaxation induces a 12.23 : 1 directional survival-error split (\kappa_{T_1} = (3\pi - 8)/(3\pi + 8) \approx 0.081767), whereas time-symmetric X rotations maintain an exact 1 : 1 balance (\kappa_{T_1} = 1). Across all completely positive Markovian generators, coupling between non-unital drift and unital diffusion enforces a selectivity bound \kappa_\star = (\pi - 2\sqrt{2})/(\pi + 2\sqrt{2}) \approx 0.052456 (19.06 : 1) for time-independent single-qubit \pi swaps. We apply this framework to Gaussian and derivative-removal-by-adiabatic-gate (DRAG) waveforms on superconducting transmons and trapped-ion qubits, extend the analysis to finite damping, pulse dwell, colored thermal baths, and qutrit leakage, and construct two-branch differential lock-in protocols that isolate directional error splits immune to first-order state-preparation and measurement errors.
papers.authors: Amritash Patra

papers.title: Holographic Einstein rings of a covariant quantum corrected AdS black hole
papers.abstract: We investigate holographic Einstein rings in a covariant quantum corrected Schwarzschild--AdS$_4$ spacetime using a massless scalar probe. At fixed horizon radius $r_h$, the deformation parameter $\zeta$ leaves the metric mass parameter, coordinate surface gravity, and photon sphere radius unchanged, while increasing the photon potential maximum and the asymptotic lapse coefficient $A=1+\zeta^2$. The critical coordinate impact parameter approaches $A^{-1/2}$ for large black holes, whereas the corresponding incidence angle in the normalized boundary frame approaches $\pi/2$. Ray tracing and local WKB barrier data recover the same geometric scale. Quasinormal spectra computed with AdS boundary conditions provide a comparison at finite multipole number. These results separate the finite radius effect of the deformation from the change in boundary time normalization.
papers.authors: Zhenglong Ban, Xiaomei Liu, Rong-Jia Yang

papers.title: Resonance Induced Chaos of Charged Particles Around a Magnetized, Periodically Time-Conformal Reissner-Nordstrom Black Hole with Quintessence
papers.abstract: Astrophysical black holes are never strictly static: accretion, mergers, and gravitational radiation drive a slow evolution of their geometry. We model this evolution through a periodic time-conformal deformation, $\Omega(t)=1+\epsilon\sin(\omega_d t)$, of a Reissner--Nordstr\"om black hole surrounded by quintessence, and study the resulting onset of chaos for charged test particles. The deformation converts the integrable static spacetime into a periodically driven nonlinear Hamiltonian system, so that the transition from regular to chaotic motion can be related to the breakdown of an approximate Noether symmetry. The resulting two-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian system is solved using an adaptive high-order Runge--Kutta integrator, while the dynamical behaviour is analysed through Poincar\'e sections, bifurcation diagrams, the largest Lyapunov exponent, and the Smaller Alignment Index (SALI). Our results show that the onset of chaos is controlled primarily by nonlinear resonance rather than by the magnitude of any individual parameter. Chaos grows with the conformal amplitude $\epsilon$ through resonance overlap, while the magnetic field $B$ acts non-monotonically: it produces chaos near the field strength at which the radial frequency matches the drive, and suppresses it at stronger fields by detuning. The small-divisor structure of the approximate Noether symmetry predicts the magnetic threshold without free parameters ($B_c\simeq0.011$ against the measured $0.012$), and reproduces the conformal threshold once a single coupling constant is fixed. In contrast, the quintessence parameter mainly facilitates particle escape by reducing the confining potential barrier, providing a distinct non-resonant route to the breakdown of regular motion.
papers.authors: Israr Ali Khan

papers.title: Finite Energy, Event Horizons, and a Universal Bound on the Singularity Order in Born--Infeld-type Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate an interpolated Maxwell--Born--Infeld theory bridging the Maxwell and Born--Infeld limits. In the electrostatic sector the total energy is finite, and remains bounded above even as the theory approaches the Maxwell limit. We construct the electrically charged black hole, whose black hole solution interpolates monotonically between the classical Born--Infeld and Reissner--Nordstr\"om solutions; singularity can be relegated, independently of the weight parameters. For general interpolated theories with a truncation threshold, we analyze the existence and multiplicity of event horizons and classify the horizon configurations, and for general Born--Infeld-type nonlinear structures we prove a universal lower bound on the order of the Kretschmann divergence, thereby excluding regular electric black holes.
papers.authors: Tengyang Liu

papers.title: Thermodynamics and interior structure of density-responsive regular black holes
papers.abstract: This work studies regular black holes motivated by the scalar sector of density-responsive gravity (DRG). An algebraic prescription with phenomenological local running maps a Gaussian matter profile to a diagnostic density profile. A pressure check shows that this profile does not solve the full static DRG equations. It serves only to select an effective metric family with two horizons. The extremal mass is calibrated to $M_{\min} = \sqrt{1+A/2}\,M_{\mathrm{P}} \simeq 1.006\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$, where $A=0.024$ is the historical scalar response amplitude. A fit to $\rho(r) = \rho_0\exp[-(r/r_c)^n]$ selects $n=2$. The temperature is nonmonotonic, reaching $T_H^{\max}=0.02547\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$ at $M=1.332\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$ before vanishing at $M_{\min}$. The calculation verifies the generic scaling near extremality $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{tr}}\propto(M-M_{\min})^{-1/2}$ of a static lapse diagnostic for $n=2,3,4,6$ and for the Hayward and Bardeen controls. A regulated integral of coordinate time between the horizons provides a static cavity diagnostic, not a prediction of echoes of gravitational waves. The remaining area entropy equals the area entropy already lost at $M_{\mathrm{cross}}/M_0=0.707107\simeq1/\sqrt{2}$. This geometric crossing does not establish a Page curve or unitarity. The endpoint area entropy is below $2.6\%$ of the initial Bekenstein-Hawking entropy for $M_0 = 5\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$ and below $0.03\%$ for $M_0 = 50\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$. An inverse source reconstruction confirms an isotropic core of de Sitter type but retains the pressure mismatch. An exploratory collapse calculation with an imposed bounce factor produces bounded configurations with $1-2m/r<0$ without establishing formation of the calibrated geometry. The robust results are the calibrated thermodynamics and generic scaling near extremality.
papers.authors: Martin Drobczyk

papers.title: Fourier Transform of the Scalar Propagator with Quantum Light-Cone Fluctuations
papers.abstract: We derive the Lorentzian Fourier transform of the Gaussian-smeared light-cone contribution to the scalar propagator in Krein-space quantization in terms of a Meijer $G$-function. We characterize its distributional structure, recover the massive propagator by adding the Bessel-function tail, and derive an exact expression for the massless one-loop bubble kernel using a position-space prescription.
papers.authors: M. V. Takook

papers.title: Optical Appearances and Multiple Lensed Rings of Self-Interacting Boson Stars with a Double-Well Potential
papers.abstract: As horizon-scale imaging opens a new era of strong-field gravity tests, self-interacting boson stars have emerged as compelling dark matter candidates and natural black hole mimickers. We systematically investigate the optical appearances and multiple lensed rings of such horizonless objects illuminated by a geometrically thin accretion disk. To overcome the severe numerical stiffness caused by the slowly decaying scalar tail, we introduce a robust hybrid metric reconstruction framework---seamlessly bridging an interior 6-parameter Pad\'e approximant to the exact exterior Schwarzschild spacetime via a globally $C^2$-continuous cubic spline. This ensures high-precision ray-tracing across the entire domain. For the adopted double-well potential, we identify a strict upper bound ($\phi_0 \lesssim 0.317$) for the existence of regular static solutions. Crucially, we uncover a striking non-monotonic evolution in the shadow size, driven by a macroscopic mass-amplitude turnover that is fundamentally rooted in the microphysical competition between attractive and repulsive self-interactions. Within the most compact configurations, extreme gravitational lensing generates prominent nested higher-order photon rings and distinctly separated secondary images. Furthermore, exploring the scalar potential parameter space ($\Lambda, \Gamma$) reveals a distinct diagonal gradient in the shadow size. Our findings demonstrate that next-generation VLBI observations can move beyond merely identifying horizonless objects, offering a novel geometric avenue to directly probe the microphysical couplings of dark matter scalar fields.
papers.authors: Zefang Fan, Sen Guo, Xianggao Wang

papers.title: Metric perturbations in Einstein-Hilbert gravity: An alternative perturbative formulation
papers.abstract: We derive the ordinary gauge-fixed quadratic operators of the four-dimensional Einstein--Hilbert action in exponential and inverse-metric-density variables on an arbitrary reference background. With a single nonlinear background-harmonic gauge transported through the exact field map, the density operator is the trace-reversed Lichnerowicz operator, while the exponential operator contains an additional algebraic Ricci-curvature term. This difference arises from the nonlinear transformation of the background tadpole and vanishes on Ricci-flat backgrounds; a cosmological-constant check gives the corresponding cancellation at Einstein saddles. The construction retains the exact determinant contribution and specifies the associated Faddeev--Popov operator. At the first interacting order on a flat background, we show that the two gauge-fixed cubic actions differ by a term proportional to the free field equation, and independently evaluate the same nonzero three-point coefficient in both variables, with its normalization matched to the Einstein-gravity interaction. An exact Schwarzschild configuration satisfies the same background-harmonic gauge and is stationary under unrestricted exterior variations of the gauge-fixed action. Its density and exponential reconstructions are checked together with the bulk and boundary terms; a separate radial variation illustrates the loss of an equation after imposing a restricted ansatz. These results provide an explicit comparison of established field coordinates at the classical and tree levels; quantum loop calculations additionally require a common measure, regulator and source prescription.
papers.authors: Sergey Bondarenko, Raghvendra Singh

papers.title: Kalb-Ramond black bounces: throat-blind shadows and throat-sensitive neutrinos
papers.abstract: Regularizing a black hole removes its singularity, but which observations could detect the regularized core? We address this question for a Simpson-Visser black bounce built on the power-law hairy black hole that a Lorentz-violating Kalb-Ramond background produces. Measured in the areal radius, the bounce leaves the metric function untouched and changes only the radial measure. This single fact sorts the observables into two classes. The shadow, the innermost stable orbit, orbital frequencies and gravitational redshifts are blind to the throat. The instability of the photon ring, the brightness of its subrings, the oscillation phase of neutrinos and the energy deposited by neutrino pair annihilation respond to it through one universal factor. We derive an exact law for the subring demagnification that holds for any metric function. We also show that the throat enters the weak-field neutrino phase and the light deflection with different weights, so that combined photon and neutrino lensing can separate the mass from the throat. Ray-traced polarized images of a turbulent thin disk confirm that the direct image hides the throat while the first subring reveals it. For neutrinos emitted near a stellar-mass compact object the throat reshapes the flavor survival pattern and enhances the annihilation energy deposition. Two independent computations reproduce each headline number.
papers.authors: Faizuddin Ahmed, Ahmad Al-Badawi, \.{I}zzet Sakall\i

papers.title: Electric-magnetic asymmetry of exact dyonic Euler-Heisenberg black holes: duality-blind shadows and magnetically controlled horizons
papers.abstract: Maxwell theory is invariant under electric-magnetic rotations, and the Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole depends on its charges only through the sum of their squares. The Euler-Heisenberg vacuum-polarization terms break this symmetry, and an exact dyonic Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg black hole was found recently. We ask which properties remember the breaking. Outside the photon sphere, almost none do. The metric function is even under charge exchange through first order in the coupling, the first odd term appears at second order and falls off as the tenth inverse power of the radius, and the shifts it causes in the shadow, the Lyapunov exponent, and the innermost stable circular orbit stay at a few parts per million. The core behaves differently. Any magnetic charge drives the metric function to negative infinity at the center and so forces a horizon, while an electric configuration lighter than its field energy can be horizonless. Whether an extremal limit exists is decided by one function of the charges, the maximum of the derivative of the mass function, whose critical curve reaches the origin along the electric axis and meets the magnetic axis at a closed-form value. Two independent integrations confirm every number, and the shadow is tested against the Event Horizon Telescope image of Sagittarius A*.
papers.authors: Vahideh Memari, \.{I}zzet Sakall{\i}

papers.title: Application-Oriented Evaluation of CPU/GPU Quantum Simulators: From Foundational Circuits to Quantum Chemistry
papers.abstract: Quantum computing simulators underpin the development and prototyping of quantum algorithms, yet the practical choice between competing software stacks and their CPU and GPU backends is rarely guided by application-oriented evidence. We present a systematic, quantum hardware-agnostic evaluation of two widely used stacks, CUDA-Q and Qiskit, selected as the simulators closest to production execution paths, across CPU and GPU backends, and across single- and double-precision arithmetic. The evaluation spans foundational utility circuits (GHZ-state preparation and QFT/QFT$^\dagger$ mirror circuits) through applied quantum chemistry (Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) energy estimation with standard UCCSD and a depth-reduced LCNot-UCCSD ansatz, and direct sampling on hydrogen chains up to 32 qubits). The results yield concrete selection guidance: GPU-accelerated double precision delivers consistent speedups, typically $2\times$ to $10\times$ for tractable application workloads and substantially larger at the widest circuits up to $100\times$ or more, and governs the maximum simulable system size under fixed compute memory, while CPU statevector backends and Qiskit Aer remain competitive, and at times preferable, at low qubit counts and wide but shallow circuits. We demonstrate the practical payoff of this guidance by extending an in-house developed QSCI(LCNot-UCCSD)-RBM electronic-structure workflow, previously constrained to a 16-qubit active space on a CPU, to a 32-qubit (10 electrons, 16 orbitals) active space with GPU acceleration, completing a 20-point potential-energy-surface scan of N$_{2}$ in the cc-pVDZ basis. This end-to-end evaluation establishes that the principled simulator selection translates directly into expanded scientific reach and faster algorithmic prototyping.
papers.authors: Anurag K. S. V., Ashish Kumar Patra, Afra Navas, Ruchika Bhat, Sai Shankar P., Rahul Maitra, Manas Mukherjee, Jaiganesh G

papers.title: The Klein-Gordon equation in projective geometry
papers.abstract: We discuss a geometric method by which H\"ormander's result on the asymptotics of a Klein-Gordon field, on an asymptotically flat spacetime, can be related to some partial peeling, \`a la Penrose, along an extended projective boundary, embedded in a spacetime with one dimension higher.
papers.authors: Jack Borthwick, Yannick Herfray

papers.title: B\"{a}cklund transformations of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation
papers.abstract: In this paper B\"{a}cklund transformations of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation are discussed. The B\"{a}cklund transformations are applied to rational solutions of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation, which are expressed in terms of the generalised Laguerre polynomials and generalised Umemura polynomials. Using appropriate B\"{a}cklund transformations, we derive non-unique solutions of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation in terms of modified Bessel functions. Further it is shown that there are also rational solutions in terms of generalised Umemura polynomials for the same values of the parameters, which are not special cases of the modified Bessel function solutions. The relationship between solutions of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation and solutions of the third Painlev\'{e} equation is also discussed.
papers.authors: Peter A. Clarkson, Clare Dunning, Ben Mitchell

papers.title: An Incomplete-Preference Quantum Anscombe--Aumann Representation
papers.abstract: By dropping the idea that completeness is a mandatory prerequisite for agents' rationality, this work shows how classical and quantum subjective probability attributions represent suitable preference orderings. To do so, we develop an extension of the Anscombe--Aumann framework in which acts map a finite set of states of the world into the effect interval of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, while preferences need not be complete. The construction keeps three logically distinct questions separate. First, an incomplete-preference multi-utility theorem supplies affine utility functionals. Second, finite-dimensional operator geometry determines the form of each affine functional. Third, admissibility identifies which normalised probability--state pairs are compatible with the full preference. We introduce behavioural state-independence as the natural Anscombe--Aumann interpretation of the idea that the identity of the states of the world should not affect how quantum consequences are compared. Because an incomplete preference makes this aggregate behavioural condition weaker than a utility-by-utility condition, the factorisation theorem requires a stronger, explicitly operational representation-level condition. Under that condition and Loewner monotonicity, every affine utility functional is positively affinely equivalent to a normalised utility of the form $ U_{p,\rho} (f)= \sum_{s} p(s) Tr( \rho f(s) )$. Consequently, a suitable incomplete preference relation is represented by a family of admissible pairs in $\Delta(S)\times D(H)$. We then identify a canonical maximal compatible family and show that the scalar-effect subspace carries an ordinary classical multi-utility representation, with scalar events appearing as the vertices of the scalar-act cube.
papers.authors: Cristhiano Duarte

papers.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for the Spherically Averaged Density of Atoms
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of the spherically averaged density $\widetilde \rho$ for fermionic bound states of the $N$-electron atomic Hamiltonian $H_{N,Z}$ with nuclear charge $Z$. For the density associated with an eigenfunction satisfying $H_{N,Z}\psi=E\psi$, we show that if the energy $E$ is below the bottom of the essential spectrum $\Sigma:=\inf\mathop{\rm ess. spec} (H_{N,Z})$, then $\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{\ln \widetilde \rho(r)}{r} =\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{d}{dr}{\ln \widetilde\rho(r)} =-2\alpha_0$, with $\alpha_0=\sup\{\alpha \ge 0\colon e^{2\alpha r}\widetilde \rho \in L^1(\mathbb{R}_+,r^2dr)\}$. The same is true at threshold in certain cases. Moreover, we prove $\alpha_0^2=\Sigma-E$ for the ground states of $H_{3,Z}$ with sufficiently large $Z$.
papers.authors: Yukimi Goto

papers.title: Hybrid Uncertainty in the Real Forms of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)$
papers.abstract: An optimized commutator bound can lie strictly below the quantum infimum even when its minimizing mean is realized by a quantum state. We study hybrid uncertainty, defined as the sum of pairwise products of standard deviations. For any spanning list of nonzero real linear combinations of the generators in a positive discrete series representation of $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$, the commutator bound has a unique minimizing mean, realized by a Perelomov coherent state. We prove that the optimized bound equals the infimum over states with finite second moments if and only if the symmetrized covariance matrix of the prescribed observables is diagonal in this state. When this condition fails, the quantum infimum is strictly greater than the bound; for a nonorthogonal list, we obtain an explicit positive lower bound on this gap. For irreducible spin-$j$ representations of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, we derive the exact minimum of the spectral hybrid uncertainty over states for any spanning list of spin observables. For a fixed state, we compare separate measurements made before a random target is disclosed with direct measurement of the target known in advance. For these protocols, the excess mean squared error coefficient equals twice the listed hybrid uncertainty, and its minimum over orthogonal combinations of the observables equals twice the spectral hybrid uncertainty.
papers.authors: Xiaoli Hu, Xiaoyong Yang, Naihuan Jing

papers.title: QuantumInputOutput.jl: A Julia framework for input-output theory with quantum pulses and the SLH formalism
papers.abstract: The interaction of traveling photonic pulses with quantum systems is a fundamental process for many quantum technologies such as quantum communication, control, and measurement protocols. The so-called SLH formalism, named for the triple of operators that parametrize the dynamics, in combination with virtual emission and absorption cavities provides a general toolbox to describe such processes. However, modeling open quantum systems driven by propagating quantum pulses becomes cumbersome once several components, channels, and temporal modes are involved. Here we present QuantumInputOutput, an open-source framework that automates this derivation process: first, symbolic expressions for the Hamiltonian and Lindblad operators are derived using predefined SLH rules and symbolic quantum algebra. Next, the obtained operators are converted to (time-dependent) numerical matrices or are used to obtain higher-order mean-field equations. The numerical expressions are presented in a form immediately suitable for solving the time evolution of the master equation and analyzing the output modes via correlation functions. Besides its usefulness for numerical simulations, the framework also provides a convenient tool to derive symbolic expressions for one-dimensional quantum systems such as multilevel emitters in cavities or waveguides.
papers.authors: Christoph Hotter, Orjan Ameye, Klaus M{\o}lmer

papers.title: Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations
papers.abstract: We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications. These quasi-local connections strengthen previously known quantum-channel circuit constructions based on the decay of connected correlation functions [R. Ma, V. Khemani, and S. Sang, PRX Quantum 7, 033052 (2026)], which approximately connect states within the same phase but have depths that grow logarithmically with system size. Furthermore, if the Gibbs-state path contains a product state, we prove that the single-site Glauber dynamics has a $\Omega(1)$ spectral gap independent of the system size throughout the path. This establishes Glauber-dynamics fast mixing for models that may violate the strong spatial mixing condition used in prior proofs, including (1) the $q$-state Potts model throughout the high-temperature phase for any $q$ and any finite dimension; (2) the Ising model with a longitudinal field at low temperature, with frustrating perturbations that destroy monotonicity of the dynamics; and (3) the three-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory at low temperatures comparing to a field perturbation, even though the model supports classical memories at intermediate temperatures. Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.
papers.authors: Chao Yin, Vedika Khemani

papers.title: Microcausality Bounds on Dispersion Laws
papers.abstract: Microcausality holds in any state, including those that spontaneously break Lorentz invariance, and requires the poles (and other singularities) of the retarded Green's function to satisfy $\mathrm{Im}\,\omega \le |\mathrm{Im}\,k|$ throughout the complex plane. Building on the work of Heller, Serantes, Spali\'nski and Withers, we study its consequences for dispersion relations that are linear at small $k$, like Goldstone bosons, assuming tree-level, non-dissipative dynamics. We show that microcausality is equivalent to requiring that $k \pm \omega(k)$ be typically real functions. This yields two-sided bounds on all higher-order coefficients of $\omega(k)$ in units of its radius of convergence $R$, the scale at which the linear Goldstone description breaks down. The optimal constraints are characterised by an infinite hierarchy of Toeplitz determinants. We derive analogous bounds on $\omega^2(k)$, whose radius of convergence $\tilde R$ marks the scale at which new states must appear. The bounds shrink to zero as the sound speed $c_s$ approaches 1: for a fixed higher-derivative correction, both $R$ and $\tilde R$ become parametrically smaller than naive dimensional analysis suggests. In particular, in the EFT of Inflation all higher-derivative quadratic operators must vanish as $c_s \to 1$. We test the bounds in several models: a $U(1)$ superfluid, light in a dielectric medium, photon propagation in a strong magnetic field, colour-flavour-locked quark matter, and a homogeneous solid. Finally, we extend the bounds to gapped modes.
papers.authors: Paolo Creminelli, Michael Mancini, Warin Patrick McBlain

papers.title: Bound States of Two D0-Branes and the Three-Graviton Coupling
papers.abstract: We numerically solve for the ground state of the $SU(2)$ BFSS matrix model for M-theory. This state corresponds to the zero-energy bound state of two D0-branes or, by the BFSS conjecture, to the eleven-dimensional graviton with two units of momentum along the M-theory circle. The wavefunction exhibits a strongly coupled core, as well as an asymptotic power-law tail where the D0-branes are well separated. The coefficient of this power-law decay is the three-graviton coupling, previously computed by Herderschee and Maldacena, which our numerical solution reproduces with high accuracy. We also show that this coupling is protected by supersymmetry in the matrix model, and derive its value from the non-renormalized one-loop interaction of the two D0-branes. Lastly, we provide a simple representation-theoretic argument regarding the recently proposed excited bound states of the model.
papers.authors: Sergio Sanjurjo, Themistocles Zikopoulos

papers.title: Sharp Uniform Fisher Information Bounds from Projective Designs
papers.abstract: Fixed measurements for multiparameter pure-state metrology must remain informative without knowing the input state. We quantify this requirement by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information that a measurement retains over all pure states and tangent directions. We determine the Fisher guarantees, namely lower bounds on Fisher floors, implied by projective design order alone in every dimension $d\ge 2$. These guarantees are sharp at order $t=2$ and every odd order $t\ge 3$, and finite weighted designs attain them; at even orders, our bounds are nearly tight. As the order increases, the guarantees approach one half, the single-copy quantum limit. Sampling and spectral completion of any 3-design yield, with probability $1-O(1/d)$, a measurement with linearly many outcomes and a dimension-independent Fisher floor. Such a measurement separates all pure states in Hellinger distance, so pure-state maximum-likelihood estimation from $N$ copies attains mean infidelity $O(d/N)$ uniformly over pure states, optimal up to a universal constant factor.
papers.authors: Zhiyao Yang, Bowen Xiao, Huangjun Zhu

papers.title: Global Fit Inference for LISA with samsara++
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe a superposition of gravitational-wave signals, requiring joint inference of an unknown number of sources, parameters, and instrumental noise. To disentangle these contributions, that overlap in both time and frequency, a Global Fit (GF) analysis is needed. We present samsara++, a C++/CUDA sampler designed to address this trans-dimensional GF problem. Building on the continuous-time MCMC framework of samsara, the algorithm combines birth-death processes for adding and removing sources, with mutation moves for parameter estimation. Birth and death are selected through posterior-dependent rates. Shared-memory parallelism, incremental likelihood updates, and indexed storage reduce the computational and memory costs, while parallel tempering improves the exploration of multimodal posteriors. We assess the performance using simulated one-year LISA datasets containing Galactic double white dwarf binaries and stationary Gaussian instrumental noise. Analyses of populations containing 143 and 866 binaries start from empty source models, without preliminary searches or proposals tailored to the injected population. These tests demonstrate source reconstruction and catalog generation, highlighting, at the same time, the importance of source-count, overlapping signals, and incomplete mixing on joint source and noise inference. Then we perform a separate stress test, initialized at the injected parameters, exploring a population of 16,435 binaries, corresponding to 131,480 source parameters. This run completes 15 million iterations in approximately 16 hours using about 3 GB of RAM. All together, these benchmarks show the computational feasibility of birth-death sampling for large Galactic-binary populations, and provide a foundation for extending samsara++ toward a comprehensive LISA global fit.
papers.authors: Lorenzo Valbusa Dall'Armi, Gabriele Astorino, Riccardo Buscicchio, Angelo Ricciardone, Walter Del Pozzo

papers.title: Gauge aspects of teleparallel gravity and Noether's second theorem
papers.abstract: We examine the gauge structure of the Teleparallel Equivalent of General Relativity (TEGR) from the perspective of Noether's second theorem. We show that diffeomorphisms and local Lorentz transformations are the gauge symmetries of TEGR, as these are the only variational symmetries that give rise to Noether identities. We then discuss the distinct roles of these two symmetries and their implications for the gauge-theoretic interpretation of gravity. Finally, we discuss consequences of these observations for the role of translations in gauge theories of gravity and the coupling of matter in TEGR. In particular, we demonstrate that the matter coupling prescription is uniquely determined and coincides with that of general relativity, including in the case of spinor fields.
papers.authors: Sebastian Brezina, Martin Kr\v{s}\v{s}\'ak

papers.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
papers.abstract: Symmetry is a foundational principle of physics: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the coordinate frame, unit system, or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet today's leading neural surrogates lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation), rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs. Because the boundary determines the interior solution, ISLA encodes the posed boundary once into learned slices and evaluates arbitrary interior points independently through a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel. Inputs are nondimensionalized in scales computed from the boundary, sums over boundary cells are area-weighted quadratures that converge under mesh refinement, and geometry enters only as distances and relative angles to equivariant slice anchors, making the model equivariant to rigid motions and reflections up to optional token subsampling and tree clustering. On AeroZoo, 2,816 3D flows spanning diverse geometries, poses, physical scales, and boundary conditions, ISLA's mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 1.9 and 2.2 times lower than any baseline's. On full AirfRANS, ISLA is second only to an explicit boundary-integral network (GLOBE), with errors at least 1.6 times lower than Transolver's and GeoTransolver's in every field.
papers.authors: Peter Sharpe

papers.title: Numerical tests of chiral fermion weights with $\eta$-invariant phases in the 3450 model
papers.abstract: We test numerically a recently proposed prescription for coupling continuum chiral fermions to interpolated lattice gauge fields, in which the fermion weight has a Pauli-Villars (PV) regularized magnitude and a phase given by an Atiyah-Patodi-Singer (APS) $\eta$-invariant in one higher dimension. We use the anomaly-free two-dimensional $U(1)$ theory with left-handed charges $3,4$ and right-handed charges $5,0$, whose torus determinant is known exactly. At zero magnetic flux, with gauge fields interpolated from lattice links, the Polyakov loops evaluated on a $16\times16$ grid of flat connections agree with the exact values within $0.04\%$, whereas omitting the APS phase substantially reduces them to about $3\%$ of the exact result. The vacuum-polarization response yields an induced mass $m/e=2.82089$, close to $5/\sqrt{\pi}=2.82095$. At unit flux, where zero modes make the determinant vanish, we calculate a twelve-point correlator on a cylinder with the generalized APS boundary condition. For three smooth backgrounds its magnitude agrees with the exact result within $0.8\%$. Without the $\eta$-invariant its phase deviates by $1.8$-$3.0$ mrad, and with it by $0.2$-$0.5$ mrad. The phase of each charged fermion changes by $15$-$46$ mrad when the gauge field is extended differently into the third dimension, but the change cancels to below $0.2$ mrad in the anomaly-free combination.
papers.authors: Tatsuhiro Misumi

papers.title: A Probabilistic Characterization of the Ideals of Resolvent Algebras
papers.abstract: We characterize the ideal theory of Buchholz for resolvent algebras in probabilistic terms. Regarding closed two-sided ideals as kernels of representations, we pass from representations to the Gelfand--Naimark--Segal representations of states, and describe the singular, trivially regular, and regular parts, which Buchholz gives through the one-particle space, by the behavior of the corresponding probability measures of the fields. On an isotropic subspace, the resolvent algebra is a commutative $C^{\ast}$-algebra whose states correspond to probability measures, and this correspondence carries the description further to sub-$\sigma$-algebras. Starting from Bose--Einstein condensation of the free Bose gas with its direct integral representation and from the treatment of the infrared singularity of the van Hove model, we connect the ideal-theoretic and the probabilistic arguments. Since the ideals carry physical information in these arguments, we show that the corresponding sub-$\sigma$-algebras and their inclusions carry this information in correspondence with the ideals.
papers.authors: Yoshitsugu Sekine

papers.title: Communication inequalities: robust quantum advantage, measurement testing and dimension witnessing with minimal setups
papers.abstract: Communication scenarios (CS) are arguably the simplest setting in which quantum behaviors can be observed. Yet, in contrast to Bell scenarios or prepare-measure scenarios with shared randomness, no general method is known to separate classical and quantum statistics. Here we close this gap by deriving dimensional inequalities to separate classical and quantum statistics in CS. These depend only on four parameters of the input-output statistics, corresponding to correlated and anticorrelated events. Under dimensional assumptions, saturating one of the inequalities certifies SIC-POVMs with analytical noise robustness. The inequalities also yield a dimension witness for both correlated and anti-correlated statistics, without the need of measurement incompatibility.
papers.authors: Albert Rico, Mani Zartab, Javier Fern\'andez, John Calsamiglia, Some Sankar Bhattacharya

papers.title: Relaxation of Quantum Observables in a 4D Black Hole that forms from Collapse of a Null Shell
papers.abstract: The vacuum polarization and luminosity are computed in a four-dimensional spacetime where a spherically symmetric null shell contracts to form a black hole. This is done by computing the contribution of the spherically symmetric modes of a massless minimally coupled scalar field to the quantities $\la \phi^2 \ra_{\rm in} - \la \phi^2 \ra_U$ and $L_{\rm in} - L_U$. Here the subscript ``in'' denotes the {\it in} vacuum state for the null shell spacetime and the subscript ``U'' denotes the Unruh state in Schwarzschild spacetime. The computation is done outside the null shell and outside the event horizon where the spacetime geometry is the Schwarzschild geometry. It is found that, as expected, these differences approach zero at late times. However, they do so significantly more slowly than in the two-dimensional case where there is no scattering of the mode functions. In both cases, the difference is dominated by a quasinormal mode at intermediate times and a tail term at late times that decays quartically in time. For the luminosity difference, an analytic calculation verifies the late-time result for the tail term.
papers.authors: Shohreh Gholizadeh Siahmazgi, An{\i}l Zengino\u{g}lu, Paul R. Anderson, Alessandro Fabbri

papers.title: Exact transformation-optics representation of the Ellis wormhole and limits of finite-device scattering emulation
papers.abstract: We derive a global isotropic representation of the ultrastatic Ellis wormhole and establish which features of its electromagnetic response can, and cannot, be reproduced by a finite device. An orientation-preserving coordinate map sends the signed proper-radial line to a punctured Euclidean chart with refractive index $n(\rho)=1+a^2/(4\rho^2)$. Through the Pleba\'nski correspondence, this gives the exact impedance-matched continuum medium $\varepsilon_r=\mu_r=n(\rho)\mathbf{I}$ and its full vector-Maxwell operator. For the ideal two-ended geometry, we derive the electromagnetic radial operator, establish its spectral properties, and express its scattering amplitudes through Jost solutions and Wronskians. Nonzero transmission into the second asymptotic end implies $|R_{\rm id}|<1$ at every real frequency, whereas a regular, lossless finite one-port has unit-modulus reflection. The reverse triangle inequality therefore yields a strictly positive lower bound on the complex reflection-amplitude mismatch. This theorem applies to the stated lossless single-port class and is not extended to lossy or multiport realizations. We compute converged multipole scattering data and establish the low-frequency threshold scaling $|T_L|^2\propto(\omega a/c)^{4L+2}$, with coefficients independently validated for $L=1,2,3,4$. The transmission cross section tends to $\pi a^2$, while the ideal profile's total scattering cross section has a logarithmic forward divergence. We also construct a smooth finite-shell target and derive an exact finite-band constitutive-error formula for a calibrated passive Lorentz model. The constitutive benchmark is kept distinct from scattering equivalence throughout.
papers.authors: Abdullah Guvendi, Claudio Furtado, Omar Mustafa

papers.title: Holographic dual of the 2d Ising model
papers.abstract: We propose a holographic dual of the 2d Ising model on a torus as the Turaev-Viro TQFT on a solid torus. The bulk spacetime is divided into the ``core'' region and the ``sandwich'' region. The core region prepares a defect state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on the topological boundary $\mathbb{D}$. The sandwich region computes the Turaev-Viro state sum $\langle\mathcal{D}|\Pi|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ between the state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on $\mathbb{D}$ and the state $|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ on the physical boundary $\mathbb{B}$. The fusion diagram (or string-net) $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{B}$ is given by the Aasen-Fendley-Mong construction. There is also a ``bedding surface'' $\mathbb{S}$ between $\mathbb{D}$ and $\mathbb{B}$, and the height variables (or Ising spins inside/outside of the domain wall) are naturally living on $\mathbb{S}$. The bulk spacetime is discretized by the 2-skeleton $P$ which interpolates $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{F}$. When the defect $\mathcal{D}$ is absent, the 2-skeleton $P$ ends on the bedding surface $\mathbb{S}$ and $P$ is interpreted as the bulk worldsheet of the string-net $\mathcal{F}$.
papers.authors: Kazumi Okuyama

papers.title: Sensing frequencies at the discrete Grover-Heisenberg limit using a single qubit
papers.abstract: We consider a fundamental quantum sensing task: detecting weak oscillating fields with unknown strength and frequency. Recent work by Allen et al. established a fundamental lower bound on the required sensing time, which they named the "Grover-Heisenberg limit", and gave a protocol attaining this limit. The protocol relies on auxiliary qubits, which are used to run Grover's algorithm as a subroutine, leaving open the question of whether a single sensing qubit can achieve the same scaling. We show that a single qubit suffices for a discrete version of this problem in which the frequency belongs to an arbitrary, but known, finite set of candidate frequencies. Our protocol's sensing time grows only as the square root of the number of candidate frequencies. We prove that this square-root dependence, which we refer to as the "discrete Grover-Heisenberg limit", is optimal in the worst case.
papers.authors: Boyang Chen, Andrea Coladangelo, Jerry Li, Haocheng Zhang

papers.title: Low-energy spectral-window truncation for compact U(1) lattice gauge theory
papers.abstract: We establish a nonasymptotic electric-flux truncation bound covering the entire vacuum-relative low-energy spectral window of the original pure compact $U(1)$ lattice Hamiltonian. Formulated on a three-dimensional periodic cubic lattice with $N\geq3$ sites per direction at $\theta=0$ in the gauge-invariant zero-global-flux sector, our factorial-squared tail-norm estimate applies uniformly to every normalized vector in the window without requiring physical eigenvalue isolation, a window-edge gap, or nondegeneracy, and carries no window-dimension factor. This uniform control bounds ordered low-energy eigenvalue and excitation-energy errors while governing finite-time hard-wall evolution initialized from each state's normalized projection. Within this model, an analytic finite-volume strong-coupling construction certifies a nonvacuum band and an order-one coherent plaquette signal change that persists under a specified finite cutoff. The window estimate further provides precision-dependent sufficient cutoffs, a polar-decomposition linear isometric encoding for reference-entangled inputs, and readout bounds for the local electric square. Under lattice refinement at fixed positive bare coupling, physical volume, window width, and evolution duration, cutoffs scaling as $\beta\log N/\log\log N$ with $\beta>2$ drive the state and bounded-readout truncation errors to zero.
papers.authors: Yi Liang

papers.title: Maximal Violation of Mermin Inequality for Commuting von Neumann Algebras and Multipartite Vacuum Entanglement in QFT
papers.abstract: Summers and Werner proved that Bell inequalities are violated maximally and generically in the vacuum of a relativistic quantum field theory in [S. J. Summers and R. Werner, Commun. Math. Phys. 110 (1987), 247-259]. Their criterion concerns two-party case, that is, there are two algebras of quantum observables: one algebra and its commutant. In this case, the maximal CHSH value is converged to in every normal state exactly when the algebra is strongly stable. In the paper, we study the corresponding question for three and more mutually commuting von Neumann algebras. We focus on the multipartite Mermin inequalities instead of CHSH ones. For the tripartite Mermin functional we show that maximal violation in every normal state is equivalent to the existence of a common sequence of asymptotic GHZ stabilizers. Strong stability of each local factor is an necessary condition for maximal violation, and a joint embedding of an infinite GHZ tensor product is sufficient. Counterexamples show that strong stability and type III_1 of the individual algebras, even together with tripartite duality, do not suffice to arrive at the maximal violation. The results are also extended to n>=3 parties.
papers.authors: Kan He, Jinchuan Hou, Shuyuan Yang, Bingke Zheng

papers.title: Sample complexity of learning fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states with single-copy and entangled measurements
papers.abstract: With single-copy measurements, every mixed fermionic Gaussian state on $m$ modes, pure modes included, is learned to trace distance $\epsilon$ from $\Theta(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies, with no logarithmic factor, against the known $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$ for collective measurements. We prove the upper bound, resolving Conjecture 10.1 of arXiv:2609.23189 (lower bound for $\epsilon\le1/3600$), and fill most open entries of the sample-complexity table of fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states, for single-copy, $k$-copy and collective measurements. With blocks of $k$ copies, the covariant highest-weight measurement of arXiv:2611.07271, read out through the Weyl-shift estimator, is exactly unbiased for every state; it gives $\Theta(\max\{m^3/k,m^2\}/\epsilon^2)$ in Frobenius norm on all states and in trace distance on every class at a fixed distance from the pure boundary. The gain $1/k$ ($k\le m$) away from the pure boundary, against $1/\sqrt k$ on cold number-conserving states, is therefore attained. Learning a quadratic fermionic Hamiltonian in Frobenius norm from its Gibbs state at bounded $\beta\|h\|$ has the same rate. For bosonic Gaussian states with bounded covariance, any displacement and squeezing, and occupations $n_1\le\dots\le n_m$, $O((m^2+r^3+\sum_{i,j>r}1/(n_i+n_j))/\epsilon^2)$ single-copy measurements suffice, $r$ the largest index with $r\,n_r\le2$; this is the minimax rate on dyadic-interval classes, with no spectral gap or cold-mode count assumed, and holds with no covariance bound for displaced passive states. With no bound on energy or squeezing, non-Gaussian measurements learn centred one-mode states, mixed included, from $O(\epsilon^{-2})$ and centred pure $m$-mode states from $O(m^2/\epsilon^2)$ single copies, free of the $\log\log E$ term of Gaussian measurements, and $m$-mode states from $O(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies, entangled only in a first round on blocks of $4m+6$.
papers.authors: Ron Rubin

papers.title: A dual-moment phenomenological framework for gravitational,electromagnetic and strong interactions
papers.abstract: The unification of fundamental interactions remains an outstanding open problem in fundamental physics. Most existing unification schemes rely on extra dimensions, exotic symmetries, or unobserved dynamical degrees of freedom. Here we construct a minimal classical phenomenological framework built on primitive charges and motion-induced kinetic dual moments. Gravitational, electromagnetic, and strong interactions are coherently formulated within a unified inverse-square-law structure. We postulate a universal coupling relation connecting source-charge couplings and moment-mediated couplings across these interaction sectors. Although weak-charge degrees of freedom can be formally accommodated within the formalism, full quantitative treatment of weak-interaction dynamics is left for future work. The model recovers well-established low-energy limits for planetary orbits, atomic systems, and heavy-quark hadrons. Importantly, it yields distinguishable corrections to light deflection by rapidly spinning compact objects, and three independent experimental schemes are proposed to test these predictions.
papers.authors: Zhiguang Tan, Shengjie Wang, Hua Zheng

papers.title: Challenging the hoop conjecture with spinning pancakes and baguettes
papers.abstract: Understanding when gravitational collapse produces a black hole remains a central challenge in general relativity. Black-hole uniqueness results characterize the stationary endpoint under suitable assumptions, while singularity theorems establish geodesic incompleteness in the presence of trapped surfaces and appropriate energy and global conditions. Neither, however, provides a general criterion for horizon formation. The hoop conjecture offers such a criterion by relating the enclosed mass to the compactness of a matter distribution in every direction. We construct axisymmetric families of initial data describing rotating dust and test a formulation of the conjecture adapted to this setting. We explore highly prolate and oblate configurations with both constant and differential rescaled angular-velocity profiles, including configurations near the threshold for apparent-horizon formation. We find that the conjecture holds for rotating configurations, with a coefficient within 14% of unity as in the nonrotating case, provided the quasilocal mass includes the rotational energy. If the irreducible mass of the apparent horizon is used instead, the deviations grow with spin, as they do for Kerr black holes. For horizonless configurations, the conjecture likewise holds when the mass is restricted to the energy enclosed by the matter surface, whereas using the ADM mass, which also includes rotational field energy outside the matter, leads to apparent violations of up to $\approx$25%. We also discuss the possible evolution of compact configurations without apparent horizons, their relation to weak cosmic censorship, and their implications for horizonless compact objects.
papers.authors: Robin Croft, Gerardo Garc\'ia-Moreno, Paolo Pani

papers.title: Thermodynamics of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson black holes from background subtraction
papers.abstract: The non-asymptotic flatness of the charged rotating black holes immersed in the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field causes the ambiguity in the gauge choice for the time generator and the electric potential. By using the newly established form of the integrability condition together with the gauge choice for the asymptotically flat charged rotating black holes as the initial condition, we have found that the gauge can be uniquely fixed. With this fixed gauge, we further obtain the mass and angular momentum by the background subtraction method with the Minkowski spacetime as the reference spacetime. As a result, not only is the first law of black hole thermodynamics as well as the quantum statistical relation automatically satisfied, but also both the Christodoulou-Ruffini relation and the Smarr formula are obeyed.
papers.authors: Chang-Xu Yan, Zili Mou, Yu Tian, Hongbao Zhang

papers.title: Direct product geometries in $n$-dimensional linear and quadratic gravity
papers.abstract: Direct-product spacetimes offer a tractable route to exact solutions in gravity theories beyond general relativity. We study $n$-dimensional direct-product spacetimes of $(m_1+m_2)$, $(2+m)$, and $(2+\ldots+2)$ type in linear gravity and general pure quadratic-curvature gravity, allowing the two-dimensional subspaces to have nonconstant curvature. We classify the resulting solution spaces and determine how the allowed geometries depend on the gravitational theory, the dimension, and the curvature couplings. Metrics containing two-dimensional part(s) of nonconstant curvature are governed either by algebraic conditions on a curvature profile, or, in one special class of quadratic gravity, by a differential equation. Relations governing metrics with only constant-curvature $m$ dimensional subspaces are purely algebraic. We compare the two considered theories and study relations between their solution sets. We further examine conformal relations, generalized Petrov types, and compatibility with electromagnetic sources. Four- and six-dimensional cases are analyzed in detail, and so is the Weyl squared action (that reduces to Weyl conformal gravity in $n=4$), as a particular example of quadratic gravity couplings. Explicit analytic solutions illustrating the resulting structure are presented whenever possible.
papers.authors: Petr Jizba, Tereza Lehe\v{c}kov\'{a}

papers.title: Thermochemical Rossby waves in rapid rotation: from swallowtail geometry to nonlinear selection
papers.abstract: When heat and solute both destabilise a rapidly rotating fluid, do their buoyancies add? Codensity models assume so, giving a straight onset diagonal; spherical shells show curved and kinked thresholds. We study the Busse-Simitev rotating annulus, whose normal modes obey an exact complex cubic dispersion relation. Combining the Bilharz criterion with the neutral-curve envelope yields, in the rapid-rotation limit, an explicit swallowtail wave front, in Arnold's sense, that bends the codensity diagonal into smooth and then kinked thresholds as the diffusivity ratio decreases. Its cusp edges lie inside the unstable domain and its exposed kink ends at the swallowtail singularity; these are singularities of wave-number selection, without coalescence of temporal eigenvalues, and the swallowtail diffusivity ratio has analytical small- and large-Prandtl-number limits. At a kink, broad, fast thermal and narrow, slow compositional Rossby waves become neutral together; hidden arcs mark the birth and merger of unstable wave-number bands. The same geometry enters nonlinear selection: mean-scalar feedback factors through neutral-arc normals and scalar responses, so the mean-profile coexistence margin is positive at every corner of the leading front and vanishes quadratically with the kink angle as the waves merge. Complete cubic coefficients predict robust coexistence at a reference corner and a narrow bistable interval near merger. Periodic-cell simulations away from merger confirm the coexisting waves and their invasion thresholds.
papers.authors: Oleg N. Kirillov

papers.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
papers.abstract: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms can only be evaluated by classical computers on restricted or small instances. Here we demonstrate automated discovery of quantum programs beyond these regimes including order-of-magnitude improvements on scientific applications. To achieve this, we build a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover in which Gemini 4 agents synthesize novel programs against formal problem specifications and verify their correctness and cost. Agent teams collaborate, sharing results and knowledge through wikis and discussing ideas at organized conferences. Our results improve on prior baselines for parallel search (up to 2.57x), quantum arithmetic (290x), and simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug-metabolism by 12x, 8x and 2.5x respectively. Combining human and artificial intelligence at scale, under the rigor of mathematical proof, lets researchers design algorithms that today's classical and quantum computers cannot test, shortening the path to practical quantum computation.
papers.authors: Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg, Katerina Hristova, George Tsoukalas, Johannes Bausch, Eric Wieser, Francisco J. H. Heras, Nicholas C. Rubin, Guang Hao Low, S\'ebastien Racani\`ere, Nenad Toma\v{s}ev, Lei M. Zhang, James D. Watson, Tanuj Khattar, Aws Albarghouthi, Stavan Jain, Harun Khan, Leopoldo Sarra, Andrew W. Senior, Michael Broughton, Hussain Masoom, Sergio Boixo, Ryan Babbush, Swarat Chaudhuri, Pushmeet Kohli

papers.title: Oriented V-systems
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of an oriented $\vee$-system which gives a class of solutions of the oriented associativity equations generalising Veselov's $\vee$-system solutions of WDVV equations. An oriented $\vee$-system is a special configuration of pairs of a vector and a covector in a linear space. We show that the class of oriented $\vee$-systems is closed under taking subsystems and restrictions. We provide examples which include a multiparameter family related to imprimitive complex reflection groups.
papers.authors: Maali Alkadhem, Misha Feigin

papers.title: Self-interacting $p$-forms and the shear-free anisotropic cosmological model
papers.abstract: The cosmological principle may require more than observations demand: what is needed is isotropic expansion without vorticity. Extended Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker (eFLRW) cosmologies realise this with a non-vanishing anisotropic spatial curvature that is balanced by an anisotropic stress while the shear vanishes. Thorsrud and others investigated such scenarios for free differential $p$-forms. Here we extend the analysis to non-Abelian $p$-forms ($p=0,\dots,4$) with self interactions. The balance requires the anisotropic stress to decay as $a^{-2}$, $a$ being the cosmological scale factor, which we combine with the gauge-field continuity equation. The general results indicate that, in the presence of a potential, fine-tuning of the same is needed in order to balance the curvature. Notably, this is not the case for a $3$-form field $\underline{H}^a$ with a potential term $V(\underline{H}^2)=A+B\,\underline{H}^2$, where $A$ and $B$ are constants: in Bianchi class A, an uncharged 3-form balances the curvature with this potential without any tuning, and a charged one does so for a suitably chosen connection. This is the only candidate we have found where the potential does not require tuning. It is also an interesting candidate as it can be interpreted as a cosmological constant in combination with a dark-matter sector mimicking curvature.
papers.authors: Nicolas Hernandez (Universidad Industrial de Santander, Centro de Investigacion Cientifica y de Educacion Superior de Ensenada), Ben D. Normann (Norwegian University of Science and Technology), Yeinzon Rodriguez (Universidad Industrial de Santander, Universidad Antonio Narino)
