papers.abstract: We formulate the reduction technique for expanding the $n$-point AdS Feynman diagrams in two dimensions into the Wilson line networks. The technique applies to any $n$-point tree diagram, expressing it as several series of the matrix elements of Wilson line network operators, and employs the Wilson network expansions of the $(n-1)$-point AdS$_2$ Feynman diagrams, which can in turn be obtained using the same technique. Consequently, the complexity of this technique does not increase with $n$, provided that the expansions of the $(n-1)$-point diagrams are known. To demonstrate the reduction technique, we apply it to all topologically distinct five-point AdS$_2$ Feynman tree diagrams. The resulting expansions near the conformal boundary reproduce the known decompositions of the corresponding five-point Witten diagrams into conformal blocks.
papers.authors: V. S. Khiteev

papers.title: Optical and Dynamical Signatures of Pad\'{e} Approximated Wormholes in $f(T)$ Gravity
papers.abstract: We construct traversable wormhole solutions in the linear teleparallel model $f(T) = \alpha T + \beta$, adopting Pad\'e approximants of order [1/0] and [0/1] as shape functions together with the redshift function $\Phi(r) = -M/r$, and derive the corresponding source terms from the modified field equations. We assess the physical viability of both configurations through the energy conditions, Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equilibrium, the volume integral quantifier, thin-shell junction matching to an exterior Schwarzschild geometry, embedding diagrams, proper radial distance, the gravitational energy and the active mass. We then examine the observational signatures of each geometry by analysing equatorial null geodesics and the photon-sphere structure, computing shadow maps and radial intensity profiles, ray-tracing relativistic images of a geometrically thin accretion disc, and integrating timelike rosette orbits. Finally, we study the dynamical stability of both wormholes through a third-order WKB quasinormal-mode analysis across scalar, electromagnetic, and axial gravitational perturbations, cross-checked against time-domain evolution and the eikonal photon-sphere correspondence, and examine the parameter dependence of the mode spectrum together with the possibility of trapped-mode echoes.
papers.authors: Sneha Pradhan, Paras Balani, P. K. Sahoo

papers.title: Black Holes and Scalar Propagation in Three-Dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Gravity
papers.abstract: We derive an analytic black-hole family in three-dimensional scalar--tensor Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity with positive coupling. A single implicit equation determines the static circular metric and a scalar linear in time. We show that these solutions exhaust regular nonextremal exteriors with the stated AdS boundary conditions and a fixed nonzero coefficient of time in the scalar. The coupled metric and scalar perturbations have one propagating degree of freedom. On one branch, its kinetic coefficient is positive, its equation is hyperbolic throughout the exterior, and its bulk spatial energy is positive for perturbations of compact support. Scalar signals can cross the metric horizon outward, so exterior evolution needs information from the interior. For linear perturbations with the original metric and scalar boundary values fixed, nonzero compact initial master displacements with zero velocity can evolve only until their first contact with the AdS boundary. We derive this restriction from the original metric and scalar equations.
papers.authors: Cendikiawan Suryaatmadja

papers.title: Dynamical, thermal, and ground-state multiparameter quantum metrology: Fundamental limits and their attainability in magnetometry
papers.abstract: We study the simultaneous estimation of parameters in Hamiltonians $H_{\vec{\theta}}=H_{\vec{\theta}}^P+H^C$, with $H^C$ a control term, for unitary dynamics, thermal equilibrium, and ground states. In each case, we bound the quantum Fisher information matrix by the covariance matrix of the parameter generators, extending single-parameter bounds and identifying the conditions for saturation. At thermal equilibrium, a complementary lower bound quantifies the cost of non-commutativity. For vector magnetometry, we derive asymptotically tight bounds and identify many-body control Hamiltonians that approach them in all three settings.
papers.authors: Riccardo Pedroni, V\'ictor Izquierdo, Advay Burte, Paolo Abiuso, John Calsamiglia, Mart\'i Perarnau-Llobet

papers.title: Quantum vacuum inversion and multi-kink unbinding in the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model
papers.abstract: Quantum fluctuations can unbind a composite soliton while the correction to its mass stays small. We show this beyond perturbation theory for the multi-kinks of the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model. At one loop the vacuum at the centre of the multi-kink becomes the true vacuum at a coupling of order the classical lifting of the vacua. Tensor-network calculations of the lattice theory show that this inversion survives beyond one loop and has a continuum limit, and that the Gaussian effective potential captures it. On finite chains the multi-kink unbinds when the tension of the string of central vacuum between its two halves falls through zero
papers.authors: Jonathan Lozano-Mayo

papers.title: Unified spatiotemporal quantum states and spatiotemporal entanglement from Kirkwood-Dirac phase space
papers.abstract: The notion of a spatiotemporal quantum state extends the conventional concept of a spatial quantum state to the spatiotemporal domain. Such states are represented by unit-trace operators that encode correlations among quantum events distributed across space and time. In this work, we use the spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac phase space to provide a unified characterization of spatiotemporal quantum states. Spatiotemporal states obtained from Kirkwood-Dirac distributions are generally non-Hermitian and nonnormal; whereas those constructed from Margenau-Hill distributions are Hermitian. We provide a unification via (quasi)probabilistic mixture of Kirkwwod-Dirac spatiotemporal states which encompasses almost all existing formulations of spatiotemporal quantum states. We derive recursive expressions for spatiotemporal states and elucidate the relation between Kirkwood-Dirac nonclassicality and the temporality of spatiotemporal states. We further extend the construction to many-fold correlation functions and establish its connection with out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs). We also develop a more general unifying framework based on (quasi)probabilistic mixture of $s$-parametrized spatiotemporal states and establish their Petz time reversal and application in studying Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) condition in two-time setting. Finally, we apply this framework to characterize quantum entanglement in spacetime and analyze spatiotemporal entanglement using several complementary entropy measures.
papers.authors: Zhian Jia, Mei-Hui Xiao

papers.title: Charged Klein--Gordon modes on an Ellis wormhole: magnetic confinement and conditional Heun-polynomial solvability
papers.abstract: We study a charged Klein--Gordon field on the complete $(2+1)$-dimensional Ellis wormhole, coupled to the pullback of a uniform ambient magnetic field. The induced gauge potential is regular, whereas the intrinsic magnetic pseudoscalar reverses sign across the throat. For $\alpha_B>0$, the radial operator is unitarily equivalent to a self-adjoint one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operator with a smooth confining potential and discrete spectrum. The radial equation is reduced to confluent-Heun form, and polynomial solvability is shown to require two independent termination conditions. These conditions yield degree-zero Gaussian modes, degree-one states of both global parities, and representative degree-two even states. Exact Ellis-measure normalization is obtained for the degree-zero and degree-one modes. An independent fourth-order full-line finite-difference calculation validates the analytic benchmarks and determines the first eight eigenvalues and their parities. In the double-well regime, the forbidden-region action determines the leading semiclassical exponential of the even--odd level splitting.
papers.authors: Abdullah Guvendi, Omar Mustafa

papers.title: Optimal Joint Lower Bound for Sparse Quantum Linear System Solvers
papers.abstract: Quantum linear system solvers form one of the central algorithmic primitives in quantum computing, with applications ranging from differential equations and optimization to machine learning. Their cost is commonly measured through query complexity, which counts the number of oracle calls needed to access the input matrix. In the sparse-access model, this complexity is governed by three parameters: the condition number $\kappa$, the sparsity $s$ of the input matrix, and the target precision $\varepsilon$. The dependence on $\kappa$ and $\varepsilon$ is already well understood through the lower bound $\Omega(\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon))$, which matches the best known scaling in these parameters. Once the sparsity $s$ is included, however, the expected lower bound has long been conjectured to be $\Omega(\kappa\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon))$. Recent work by Mori et al. [Quantum Sci. Tech. 11 035063 (2026)] made an important step towards this goal by establishing the lower bound $\Omega(\kappa\sqrt{s})$ for constant error $\varepsilon$. In this work, we complete the picture and prove the full joint lower bound $\Omega(\kappa\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ in the sparse-access model, thereby establishing the anticipated dependence on all three parameters simultaneously.
papers.authors: Dhrumil Patel

papers.title: Differential equations for Dotsenko--Fateev integrals: the case of degenerate fields $\Phi_{n,1}$
papers.abstract: We study higher-order differential equations corresponding to integrals of the Dotsenko--Fateev type and associated with four-point correlation functions with degenerate fields $\Phi_{n,1}$. We determine the general structure and coefficients of the equations in terms of the integral parameters $ \{ A,B,C,g \} $. In particular, special cases of these equations in CFT are used for verification. In addition, the relationship between higher-order differential equations and hypergeometric operators is established.
papers.authors: Aleksandra Ivanova

papers.title: Chern bounds and tangent geometry of polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: We study the numerical geography and tangent geometry of very amply polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds $(X,H)$ through the positivity of the first jet bundle $J^1(H)$. Let $d=\int_X H^3$, $c=\int_Xc_2(X) H$, and $e=\int_X c_3(X)$. We obtain $e\ge-5d-c-c^2/(4d)$ by mixed intersections on $\mathbb{P}(J^1(H)^*)$, and $e\ge40d\left[(1-\frac{c}{10d})^{3/2}-1\right]$ by a volume estimate for a perturbed tautological class. In particular, the latter inequality shows $e+6c\ge0$, improving Sun's inequality $e+10c\ge0$. As consequences, we show (1) the uniform Hodge bounds $-4d-80\le h^{1,1}(X)-h^{2,1}(X)\le173d/66$, (2) the lower bound $\mathrm{deg} X^\vee\ge78$ for the dual hypersurface, and (3) the upper bound $d\le34$ in the critical case $X\subset\mathbb{P}^6$.
papers.authors: Atsushi Kanazawa

papers.title: Stringy Gauge Structures
papers.abstract: A field theory action, able to incorporate stringy gauge symmetry enhancement-breaking effects, which occur at particular points of moduli space in a heterotic string toroidal compactification framework, was previously constructed from three-point interactions and duality symmetries. Via doubled periodic coordinates and a non-commutative product, it encodes the non-Abelian structure in a background-independent form. Moduli-space dependence becomes manifest upon performing a generalized mode expansion. Here we further elaborate on this construction. In particular, we propose field transformations for the retained sectors that make up the foundations of a potential symmetry of the action and that, when mode expanded at enhancement points in moduli space, contain the usual non-Abelian gauge transformations. We also examine the covariance of the corresponding scalar derivative structures. Although the proposal must be regarded as a truncated version of a full, presently unknown field-theory description, it already encodes representations of massless and massive states containing up to one oscillator excitation. Finally, we relate the construction to gauged DFT with an extended tangent space by associating generalized Kaluza-Klein modes considered here with additional generalized-frame directions. At enhancement, their brackets reproduce the enhanced gauge algebra; away from enhancement, the same algebraic structure is recovered by rotating the Cartan basis.
papers.authors: Gerardo Aldazabal, Eduardo C. Andr\'es, Luc\'ia M. Cabrera, Mart\'in Mayo

papers.title: The Powers-St{\o}rmer-Ogata inequality for operator monotone functions
papers.abstract: We show that for any positive operator monotone function $f$ the inequality $\int_{[0,\infty)} f(t) \, \mathrm{d} \left\lVert E^{\Delta_{\varphi,\psi}}(t) \xi_\psi \right\rVert^2 + f'_\infty \varphi(1-s(\psi)) \geq \frac{f(1)}{2} \Bigl( \varphi(1) + \psi(1) - \lVert \varphi - \psi \rVert \Bigr)$ holds, where $\varphi, \psi \in \mathcal{M}_{*,+}$ are two normal positive linear functionals on a von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$, and $\Delta_{\varphi,\psi}$ is the associated relative modular operator. Choosing $f(t) = t^s$ with $s \in [0,1]$, the Powers-St{\o}rmer-Ogata inequality is recovered.
papers.authors: Markus B. Fr\"ob

papers.title: Shot noise can decide capacity comparisons of quantum models
papers.abstract: Shot noise can decide close comparisons of what quantum models appear able to learn. On an IBM processor, the standard estimate of a capacity measure, the effective dimension, placed a 48-qubit model above about 90% of classical networks with as many parameters at 256 shots per circuit. The split-shot estimate from the same data, which removes the bias of the Fisher matrix and needs no noise model, placed it above 12%. A registered run at six parameter points of a 16-qubit model repeated this: the standard estimate placed the three random points above every classical network, the split-shot estimate above 11 to 22%. In simulation the standard estimate reversed the comparison with the classical median at all 100 random points tried. The inflation is the size that shot noise predicts, and a forecast from a pilot run bounds it from above. For squared loss and a linear readout, the error of the standard parameter-shift estimate of a model's Fisher matrix is an exact polynomial in single-shot statistics. Its leading term grows with the effective rank of the matrix, so the shot budget for a stated precision follows from a pilot run; on hardware the observed errors were 0.85 to 1.09 times the predicted ones. The effective dimension can be bracketed from the data but not pinned down at a practical budget. Capacity reports should state their shot count and use the split-shot estimate.
papers.authors: Pavel Sulimov, Claude Lehmann

papers.title: Entanglement Harvesting Landscapes: A Common Computational Framework
papers.abstract: Entanglement harvesting provides an operational means of probing nonlocal correlations of quantum fields through localized detector-field interactions. Although studied in diverse spacetime backgrounds and quantum field states, existing studies largely focus on individual detector configurations. Here, we develop a unified perturbative framework for localized Unruh-DeWitt detectors, applicable to different detector trajectories and quantum field states through the corresponding Wightman function. Expressing detector responses in dimensionless variables and analytically reducing the perturbative integrals to numerically efficient representations enables systematic exploration of multidimensional harvesting landscapes and phase boundaries. We investigate inertial detectors in the Minkowski vacuum, thermal field states, and uniformly accelerated detectors undergoing Born-rigid motion. In the latter case, the detectors have different proper accelerations and different Unruh temperatures, leading to unequal local excitation probabilities. The harvested entanglement is evaluated by accounting for both local detector responses and the nonlocal exchange amplitude. Increasing temperature enhances the detector excitation probability while generally suppressing the magnitude of the nonlocal exchange amplitude. Consequently, within the perturbative Gaussian-switching framework and over the parameter range investigated, thermal effects suppress harvested entanglement and reduce the spatial extent of the harvesting region. The resulting landscapes provide a global characterization of detector-field interactions and demonstrate how temperature and observer motion reshape the competition between local detector noise and nonlocal field correlations. This framework provides an extensible methodology for investigating entanglement harvesting across relativistic quantum systems.
papers.authors: Rahul Nigam, Ujjwala Vadrevu, Akshay Kulkarni

papers.title: Absolutely Maximally Entangled States for Odd Prime Power Local Dimension
papers.abstract: An absolutely maximally entangled (AME) state is a pure state of $N$ parties with $d$ levels each whose reduced states on every subset of at most half the parties are maximally mixed. Such states provide perfect tensors and optimal quantum error-correcting codes. Determining the values of $N$ and $d$ for which they exist is one of the central problems in multipartite entanglement. For every odd prime power, $q=p^e\ge3$, we construct a stabilizer $\mathrm{AME}(2q,q)$ state and prove the existence of stabilizer $\mathrm{AME}(N,q)$ states for $N=2,3,\ldots,2q$. The construction uses a closed-form $q\times q$ bordered-circulant matrix $A_q$ over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ to generate a Hermitian self-dual maximum distance separable (MDS) code $[2q,q,q+1]_{q^2}$. These codes lie outside the generalized Reed-Solomon family, including its extended forms. In suitable local bases, the parent states yield Butson Hadamard matrices of order $q^q$ with $p$th-root entries, which become $q$-unitary after normalization. Paired projections on antipodal coordinates give all even lengths from $q+1$ to $2q$; one-party projections and standard short-length constructions complete the range. Weighted submatrices give further explicit realizations.
papers.authors: Mykhailo Hontarenko, Karol \.{Z}yczkowski

papers.title: Conformal boundary rigidity for simple Finsler metrics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the conformal boundary rigidity problem for Finsler metrics on a bounded domain. We establish stability estimates for determining the conformal factors of simple Finsler metrics in the same conformal class from their boundary distance functions. Our results provide the Finslerian version of the well-known stability estimates for Riemannian metrics.
papers.authors: Kelvin Lam, Hanming Zhou

papers.title: Entropic repulsion to the middle layer
papers.abstract: We consider $\nabla\varphi$ height functions with even and convex interaction energy $W$ on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$, which are restricted to take values in the set $\{-S, \ldots, S\}$ for some integer $S \ge 1$. We study the effect of entropic repulsion, which tends to push the spin values to the middle layer. We prove that the model has a unique Gibbs measure, with exponential decay of correlations, in the cases: (a) Dimension $d=2$ at all temperatures. (b) Dimensions $d\ge3$ at all temperatures, for a wide class of $W$ with non-increasing second derivative, including the family $W(x)=|x|^p$ for $p\in[1,2]$. (c) Dimensions $d\ge 3$ at both low and high temperatures, $T\in (0,\frac{W(1)d}{4(\ln d+\ln 8)})\cup(d W(2S),\infty]$, with the normalization $W(0)=0$. At low temperatures, our proof provides an alternative to Pirogov--Sinai methods. Conversely, we exhibit a class of even and convex interaction energies $W$ which, in high dimensions and suitable temperature regimes, have multiple Gibbs measures. Though uniqueness may fail, we show that the magnetization of every Gibbs measure lies in $(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})$. This implies the delocalization of the model restricted to take values in $\{0,1,\ldots\}$ (i.e., conditioned to lie above a floor) for all dimensions, any even and convex $W$, and all temperatures. Our methods extend to additional setups: We prove that height functions taking values in the real interval $[-1,1]$ always have a unique Gibbs measure, a result previously proved only for the quadratic interaction. For height functions taking values in $\{-S+\frac{1}{2}, \ldots, S-\frac{1}{2}\}$, $S \ge1 $ integer, we prove that the magnetization of every Gibbs measure lies in $(-\frac12, \frac12)$. The special case $W(x)=x^2$ of our results addresses questions left open in the work of Bricmont--El Mellouki--Fr\"ohlich (1986).
papers.authors: Max Mihailescu, Ron Peled

papers.title: Fractional Bose-Einstein Condensate Dark Matter Cores: Numerical GPP Solutions and SPARC Rotation Curves
papers.abstract: We investigate a fractional Bose Einstein condensate dark matter scenario in which an ultralight bosonic component forms a self gravitating core embedded in a predominantly cold dark matter halo. The stationary GPP system solved numerically beyond the TF approximation leads to energetically bound equilibrium configurations and good phenomenological fits to the selected rotation curves from 30 SPARC galaxies.
papers.authors: Akila Labadi, Mohamed Benarous, Ahmed Hocine

papers.title: The Einstein Tensor from UV-regulated Field Correlations
papers.abstract: It is known that the spacetime metric can be recovered from quantum field correlators. We extend this programme by showing that the Einstein tensor can be directly written in terms of UV-regulated field correlations. The same correlation structure also directly determines the Ricci tensor, while higher coincidence derivatives recover the connection and Riemann tensor. We further show that the renormalized stress-energy tensor can be formulated within this framework, up to the standard finite renormalization freedom. These results provide a correlation-based organization of the semiclassical Einstein equations and advance the programme of formulating spacetime geometry in terms of quantum field correlations.
papers.authors: Matheus H. Zambianco, Achim Kempf

papers.title: Late-time dark energy dynamics in $f(Q)$ gravity: A data-driven analysis
papers.abstract: The increasing precision and complementarity of late-time cosmological observations provide new opportunities to test modified gravity against the observed expansion history of the universe. The combination of DESI DR2 BAO measurements with cosmic chronometers (CC) and independent Type Ia supernova compilations provides a data-driven test of cosmic acceleration. Motivated by this progress, we investigate late-time dark energy dynamics in symmetric teleparallel $f(Q)$ gravity by adopting the power-law form $f(Q)=\beta Q^{m+1}$ and characterizing cosmic evolution through the effective equation of state (EoS) parameter. The model is constrained using CC, DESI DR2 BAO and three independent Type Ia supernova compilations, namely Pantheon+, DES-Dovekie and Union3. The inferred Hubble constant values are mutually consistent, yielding $H_0=68.0^{+2.7}_{-3.3}$, $68.2^{+2.7}_{-3.3}$ and $67.4^{+2.7}_{-3.3}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, respectively. Statistically, the proposed $f(Q)$ model yields lower $\chi^2_{\min}$ values and is favored by the AIC for all dataset combinations, whereas the BIC favors $\Lambda$CDM for the CC + DESI DR2 + Pantheon+ and CC + DESI DR2 + DES-Dovekie combinations and indicates no meaningful preference between the two models for the CC + DESI DR2 + Union3 dataset combinations. The reconstructed effective EoS characterizes the evolution of the cosmic fluid, while the deceleration parameter indicates the current accelerated expansion of the universe. Higher-order cosmographic parameters and the Statefinder and $Om(z)$ diagnostics provide complementary insights into the evolution of the cosmic expansion, while the Statefinder trajectories approach the $\Lambda$CDM fixed point in the far future. Overall, the power-law $f(Q)$ model provides a competitive description of the late-time expansion history and the observed cosmic acceleration.
papers.authors: Kshetrimayum Govind Singh, Kangujam Priyokumar Singh

papers.title: Separating perception from reasoning in vision-language models: a model-free render ceiling for crystal structures
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) often predict plausible structural labels from images without recovering the three-dimensional geometry behind them. End-to-end scores cannot tell whether an error comes from ambiguous views, lost visual information, or flawed reasoning. Multi-view 3D reconstruction faces its own trade-off: rigid symmetry priors erase genuine distortions, while unconstrained triangulation absorbs measurement outliers. We separate visual perception from structural reasoning through an inspectable 3D geometric intermediate. Its foundation is a model-free render ceiling: an exact reference for what calibrated, species-labeled projections determine, obtained by ruling out projective phantoms. Across a 1,950-structure census, every tested combination of four or five calibrated views uniquely determined the 3D sites from complete, species-labeled centroids. Against this reference, replacing images with exact text coordinates lowers the error rate of all 17 evaluated VLMs on crystals. The three frontier models gain 10.0-19.5 percentage points yet still miss 8.1-21.0% of cases. To recover geometry from imperfect observations, our symmetry-aware split reconstruction jointly estimates a symmetric base, coherent 3D physical displacements, and view-specific 2D corruption, adaptively selecting between atomic and collective distortion modes. Relative to Huber triangulation, it reduces coordinate error by 36.7% under Gaussian noise and 41.2% under corruption. Adaptive mode selection further cuts collective error up to 30.4% relative to atomic split across two external cohorts without sacrificing localized fidelity. Given reconstructed rather than Huber coordinates, downstream models improve. Geometric recovery thus becomes an explicit, testable foundation for structural understanding.
papers.authors: Can Polat, Mustafa Kurban, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban

papers.title: Operator-valued maximal $f$-divergences for completely positive maps
papers.abstract: We introduce an operator-valued maximal $f$-divergence for completely positive (CP) maps between von Neumann algebras, associated with an operator convex function $f$ on $(0,+\infty)$. The construction takes values in the extended lower-semibounded self-adjoint part of the codomain von Neumann algebra. We prove independence of the common CP upper bound used in its computation, joint subadditivity, monotonicity under unital precomposition and normal postcomposition, a martingale convergence theorem for normal CP maps, and joint lower semicontinuity in the point-$\sigma$-weak topology. For normal positive functionals, our construction recovers Hiai's maximal $f$-divergence. As a consequence, we establish its joint weak lower semicontinuity for arbitrary von Neumann algebras, answering a question left open by Hiai. For $\eta(t)=t log t$, we obtain an operator-valued Belavkin--Staszewski (BS) relative entropy. Moreover, for normal channels with $\sigma$-finite codomain, we prove that the BS channel divergence of Hollands and Ranallo coincides with the extended norm of our operator-valued divergence. Finally, we give finite-dimensional examples and obtain an explicit formula for a finite-index conditional expectation. In the BS case, this formula reduces to the logarithm of the Jones--Kosaki index.
papers.authors: Rui Okayasu

papers.title: Stationary Rotating Geometries Associated with Nonsingular Pulsating Collapse
papers.abstract: Since the first exact solutions of General Relativity (GR) were obtained, it became clear that the theory predicts a new class of compact objects: black holes. The Hawking--Penrose singularity theorems show that, under appropriate assumptions, gravitational collapse in GR leads to singular behavior. Motivated by the expectation that such regimes require physics beyond classical GR, effective approaches inspired by Loop Quantum Cosmology (LQC) and braneworld scenarios introduce high-density corrections. In this work we consider the static exterior geometry introduced by Gao, Lu, Shen, and Faraoni, associated with a comoving interior model in which the singularity is avoided through a sequence of collapse and bounce phases. Using the Newman--Janis algorithm in the Azreg-A\"inou formulation, we construct a stationary rotating exterior extension of this geometry. The resulting line element describes a stationary axisymmetric rotating spacetime whose horizon geometry, angular velocity, surface gravity, and Hawking temperature recover the Kerr and Schwarzschild limits when the quantum/braneworld correction becomes negligible ($l\to 0$). We further analyze the thermal response at fixed rotational state-space parameter, identify Davies-type singular points, and formulate an extended thermodynamic state-space relation.
papers.authors: A. D. Souza, F. A. Brito, J. Spinelly

papers.title: Nucleation and propagation of brittle fracture as a constrained energy minimization problem
papers.abstract: This paper presents a macroscopic, or continuum, theory aimed at describing when, where, and why cracks nucleate and propagate in nominally elastic brittle materials under monotonic, quasi-static, but otherwise arbitrary mechanical loads. Motivated by recent insights, the proposed sharp theory posits that: \emph{cracks nucleate and propagate exclusively in regions where the strength surface of the material is exceeded, with their evolution dictated by the minimization of the sum of the potential --- the elastic energy minus the work done by the externally applied forces --- and surface energies.} While the theory applies to materials with any elasticity (linear or nonlinear) and any material symmetry (isotropic or anisotropic), attention is restricted here to the most basic case of isotropic elastic brittle materials. For demonstration purposes, the theory is confronted with a set of nine tests that span the entire range of well-settled experimental knowledge on fracture nucleation and propagation --- the so-called ``Nine Circles of Elastic Brittle Fracture'' --- on both a hard material (a silicate glass) and a soft material (a synthetic rubber).
papers.authors: Oscar Lopez-Pamies, Farhad Kamarei, Gilles A. Francfort, Alessandro Giacomini

papers.title: Heterotic string couplings at order $\alpha'^3$ in NS-NS sector
papers.abstract: We utilize the standard T-duality procedure to derive the classical effective action of heterotic string theory at the eight-derivative order within the NS-NS sector, which comprises the metric, the \(B\)-field, and the dilaton. Starting from the minimal basis at this order, consisting of 872 even-parity and 477 odd-parity couplings, we perform a dimensional reduction on a circle and impose invariance under T-duality transformations, specifically the Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections. This invariance uniquely fixes a subset of the couplings to match those of type II theory up to an overall factor, while the remaining couplings are determined in terms of the coefficients at order \(\alpha'\). For these latter couplings, we adopt both the Metsaev-Tseytlin and Meissner schemes. Subsequently, through field redefinitions, we recast the action into a canonical form in which the dilaton appears solely through the overall factor \(e^{-2\Phi}\). In the Meissner scheme, the pure gravity sector precisely reproduces the known S-matrix results. In both schemes, the pure gravity terms can be expressed as the double trace \((\Tr(R^2))^2\), and when combined with the corresponding Yang-Mills terms \((\Tr(F^2))^2\), they take the unified form \((\Tr(R^2-F^2))^2\), as anticipated in the literature.
papers.authors: Alireza Pahlavan, Mehdi Ameri, Mohammad R. Garousi

papers.title: Quantum annealing through a first-order phase transition: Field theory approach
papers.abstract: Unlike second-order phase transitions, a first-order transition has a stage, in which a system is trapped in a metastable state. The decay of this state leads to abundant excitations over the ground state. We present a field theory for kinetics of defects emerging during quantum annealing computations. This theory predicts several power laws for the error generation rate during quantum annealing either through or near the first-order phase transition. Sharp changes between the power exponents are predicted for continuous parameter changes. Observation of this behavior would be a signature of first-order critical points and could help identify and avoid them for better computations. The driven Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model (LMGm) serves as the minimal model of interacting Ising spins that demonstrates this behavior.
papers.authors: Diego Andr\'es Rivera Orona, Predrag Puno\v{s}evac, Nikolai A. Sinitsyn

papers.title: Black hole apparent horizons become comoving with the universe
papers.abstract: It has been shown that static black hole event horizons cannot exist in time-dependent backgrounds without becoming naked singularities. In light of this, we are left with the question ''how does a black hole horizon evolve in an expanding universe?'' Here we offer a solution to this puzzle by showing that spherically symmetric black hole apparent horizons tend to become comoving, thus confirming the necessity of a cosmological coupling and raising intriguing possibilities for the early growth of black holes.
papers.authors: Valerio Faraoni, Massimiliano Rinaldi

papers.title: A Buchdahl solution generator for Einstein-sigma gravity and multiscalar-tensor gravity
papers.abstract: Buchdahl transformations provide a geometric route from vacuum spacetimes to scalar-field solutions. We formulate this mechanism as a target-covariant solution generator for Einstein gravity coupled to nonlinear sigma models in $D>3$ dimensions. On any connected region in which a Ricci-flat seed admits a non-null hypersurface-orthogonal cyclic coordinate with fixed-sign nonzero norm, the logarithm of that norm defines a Buchdahl potential $\Sigma$. A one-parameter redistribution of the cyclic norm then generates the exact Ricci source $R_{AB}=C_D(\beta)\partial_A\Sigma\partial_B\Sigma$, with $C_D(\beta)=\frac{D-2}{D-3}(1-\beta^2)$, while $\Sigma$ remains harmonic in the deformed metric. Composing $\Sigma$ with an affinely parametrized geodesic of a non-degenerate target metric whose squared speed is $C_D(\beta)$ therefore yields an exact Einstein--sigma-model solution. For positive-definite targets, the corresponding pullback condition also implies that the nontrivial scalar map has one-dimensional image; for indefinite targets, the geodesic ansatz remains a sufficient solution-generating sector but need not exhaust all possible realizations of the same rank-one spacetime source. Through the Einstein/Jordan-frame correspondence, the construction gives vacuum tensor-multiscalar solutions as well. We illustrate the unified generator with flat, spherical, hyperbolic and axion-dilaton targets and with Tangherlini, Weyl, Kasner, Rosen-wave, Gowdy, Kaluza-Klein bubble and C-metric seeds. The result separates cleanly the geometric Buchdahl source from its target-space realization and extends this rank-one cyclic sector across static, cosmological, wave and accelerating geometries.
papers.authors: David S. Pereira, Francisco S. N. Lobo, Jos\'e Pedro Mimoso

papers.title: Searching for symmetric mass generation with staggered fermions in four dimensions
papers.abstract: We conduct numerical simulations to map out the phase diagram and critical behavior of a lattice Higgs model composed of two massless staggered fermion fields forming a doublet under a global $SU(2)$ and coupled to a scalar field in the adjoint representation of the group. The scalar action consists of a potential comprising quadratic and quartic terms and a scalar kinetic term. At fixed quartic coupling we explore a two-dimensional parameter space finding a massless symmetric phase at weak coupling and a massive symmetric phase (SMG phase) at strong coupling. An intermediate anti-ferromagnetic phase separates these two regimes. These results are consistent with leading order weak and strong coupling expansions. We find that the critical lines bounding the intermediate phase merge at a unique point where all fermion bilinear condensates vanish but fermion susceptibilities diverge as non-trivial powers of the lattice size. We conjecture that this merged point corresponds to a multicritical point and may describe a phase consisting of a condensate of certain topological defects.
papers.authors: Nouman Butt, Simon Catterall, Gwen Hartshaw, Anna Hasenfratz

papers.title: Gravitational Waves from Green's Function Decomposition for a Kerr black hole: I. Equatorial ISCO Plunge
papers.abstract: We present a decomposition of the Kerr Green's function in the time domain, motivated by the frequency-domain split previously studied in the Schwarzschild limit. We show that the identification of a quasinormal-mode contribution, a direct part, and a late-time tail is still available, where the split times are determined by the black hole spin and positions of the emitter and receiver. We have checked this Green's function with time-domain Teukolsky numerical simulations and find excellent agreement. We also apply this decomposed Green's function in the time domain to a model problem with a test particle plunging into a Kerr black hole. The dynamically excited direct wave and quasinormal modes are obtained by convoluting the Green's function with the particle's source term, which may be viewed as the first order in mass ratio of a spinning black hole ringdown.
papers.authors: Junquan Su, Neev Khera, Abhishek Chowdhuri, Marc Casals, Huan Yang

papers.title: Information-Calibrated Quantum Diffusion: Aligning Forward Noise with Reverse Recoverability
papers.abstract: Quantum diffusion models typically parameterize forward corruption by raw channel strength, even though this parameter does not directly quantify how much ensemble information is erased or how difficult the corresponding reverse problem is. We introduce the classical--quantum information decrement $\Delta_t=I(X{:}Q_{t-1})-I(X{:}Q_t)$ as an intrinsic diffusion coordinate that links forward noise allocation to reverse recoverability. Along depolarization, equalizing $\Delta_t$ yields the unique minimax discretization of the forward information loss, while universal recoverability gives the same quantity an operational interpretation as a physically attainable local recovery budget. We further show that such local calibration is not sufficient for stochastic generation: models can satisfy the same recovery criterion while producing substantially different state distributions. This motivates a stochastic learner that combines information-calibrated recovery constraints with distribution matching. We establish finite-sample calibration and compositional trace-Wasserstein control for the resulting learner. Controlled quantum experiments validate the predicted information--recovery alignment, show that the recovery constraints improve local inversion, and confirm the complementary role of distribution matching in endpoint generation. The resulting framework also achieves stronger endpoint trace-Wasserstein performance than an official QuDDPM implementation with fewer trainable parameters. Overall, our work provides a unified information-theoretic principle for designing forward schedules, calibrating reverse steps, and separating physical recovery from generative coverage in quantum diffusion.
papers.authors: Qipeng Qian, Jialiang Jin, Shihao Wang Yuntao Qian

papers.title: Robust Quantum Extremal Numbers
papers.abstract: Absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states have attracted extensive attention because of their fundamental role and applications in quantum information. When an AME state does not exist, an extremal maximally entangled (EME) state is a pure multipartite state that maximizes the number of subsystems of size $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ whose reduced states (obtained by tracing out all other parties) are maximally mixed. We study this maximum and extend the problem to a robust setting, in which small deviations from maximal mixing are allowed. We quantify these deviations using the purity of each reduced state and derive bounds by summing the deviations over selected groups of subsystems or over all subsystems of the target size. Local inequalities lead to combinatorial bounds based on forbidden hypergraphs and Tur\\'an-type counting, improving robust bounds for several general families of multipartite systems. Global inequalities, combined with combinatorial arguments and linear programming, determine the fourth and fifth known quantum extremal numbers: the maximal counts are 112 for nine qubits and 200 for ten qubits. We further show that these counts remain unchanged in the robust setting for eight-, nine-, and ten-qubit systems when the allowed deviations from maximal mixing are below $1/5$, $1/143$, and $1/16$, respectively. These results provide a unified framework for determining exact and robust bounds on the number of maximally mixed reduced states.
papers.authors: Wanchen Zhang, Zicheng Han, Xiande Zhang

papers.title: Quantum Bicycle LDPC Codes with High $kd^2/n$ from Divisor-Driven Search
papers.abstract: Bicycle (two-block circulant) quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC)codes include some of the best known small quantum codes, yet their design has relied on group-algebra formulations in which the dimension and distance are accessible only through matrix computation. We show that in the cyclic case the construction collapses into the polynomial ring $\F_2[x]/(x^{l}-1)$: self-orthogonality is automatic, the quantum dimension is read off from a polynomial gcd, and the minimum distance is certified exactly through the Calderbank correspondence to additive codes over $\F_4$, turning code search into an algebraically pre-filtered enumeration that reaches parameter regimes poorly covered by existing tables. A computer search based on this framework recovers the short codes $[[42,12,4]]_2$ and $[[62,12,4]]_2$ and produces a family of codes with competitive figure of merit $kd^2/n$, including $[[66,20,7]]_2$ with $kd^2/n=14.85$, above the bivariate bicycle code $[[144,12,12]]_2$ ($kd^2/n=12$) at less than half the block length, together with $[[46,2,8]]_2$, $[[66,2,9]]_2$, $[[66,4,8]]_2$, $[[66,6,8]]_2$ and, at $n=90$, $[[90,16,7]]_2$, $[[90,18,6]]_2$, $[[90,20,6]]_2$. An exhaustive census at $n=48$ delineates the boundary of this picture: we exhibit a $[[48,10,6]]_2$ code from a minimal $48$-element group (the Aydin--Tamo--Barg realization uses $72$ elements), and prove that distance $5$ forces a stabilizer-rank loss, which excludes $[[48,10,5]]_2$ from the weight-$8$ symmetric coset family. The framework thus opens a systematic route to bicycle-type quantum LDPC codes beyond the reach of group-theoretic searches, and identifies exactly where genuinely coset-theoretic phenomena begin.
papers.authors: Liangdong Lu, Guanmin Guo, Yang Liu, Ruipan Yang

papers.title: Time-periodic solutions of the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system with a general external force in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract:
This paper is concerned with the time-periodic solutions of the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (VPB) system with a given time-periodic external force in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^3$, where the force is allowed to be non-potential. For the purpose, we first study the Cauchy problem around global Maxwellians, proving the global existence of small-amplitude solutions in a hybrid function space that combines the low-frequency Besov framework for the forced Boltzmann equation with a corresponding control of the self-consistent electric field. One key point occurs to the nonlinear Vlasov force $-
abla_{x}\phi \cdot 
abla_{v}f +  rac{1}{2}v \cdot 
abla_{x}\phi f$ at low frequencies. Rather than treating it as a generic source term, we exploit the Poisson equation and macroscopic balance laws to recover the structural cancellation required for the VPB semi-group estimates, which combined with high-frequency energy estimates and weighted microscopic propagation, yields a closed global well-posedness theory. We further prove uniform stability of the difference of two small-amplitude solutions driven by the same force with respect to distinct initial data. As a consequence of those results, for the time-periodic problem where the external force is time-periodic, we are able to make use of Serrin's method to establish the existence of a unique time-periodic solution of the same period together with its large time asymptotic stability. Our result also gives the existence and stability of stationary solutions when the external force is time-independent.
papers.authors: Renjun Duan, Jinkai Ni, Tong Yang

papers.title: Interacting Galilean and Finite-Energy Carroll Fermions
papers.abstract: We develop a common similarity-transformation framework for Galilean and Carrollian Dirac contractions, encompassing L\'evy--Leblond and magnetic Carroll spin-half systems. Explicit field maps relate free formulations with different mass and energy parametrizations. We obtain the complete five-parameter family of derivative-free Hermitian quartic potentials for a pair of Grassmann-odd Pauli spinors, invariant under rotations, a common $U(1)$, and triangular boosts. Higher-order and color-mixed interactions admit exact classical solutions. An independent pairing channel generates derivative interactions upon exact auxiliary elimination and sources otherwise absent Carroll spinor components. Quartic deformations of a Galilean fermionic gauge theory yield algebraic or spatial differential equations while preserving a local phase symmetry. Nambu--Jona-Lasinio contractions provide relativistic origins for selected channels.
papers.authors: Pulastya Parekh, Aditya Sharma, Mauricio Valenzuela

papers.title: Hidden Supersymmetry in Wigner-Yang Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: We consider a quantum system on the real line obeying a deformed Heisenberg algebra. This deformation was originally proposed by E.P. Wigner in 1950 when establishing the non-uniqueness of the canonical commutation relations implied by the equations of motion. An explicit coordinate representation was subsequently provided by L.M. Yang in 1951 and in essence is identical in form with Dunkl's difference-differential operator introduced in 1989 in connection with root systems of reflection groups when limited to the group $Z_2$ acting on the real line. Under certain conditions such quantum systems exhibit a supersymmetric (SUSY) structure where the reflection operator acts as the grading operator. We present a generalisation of Yang's representation by first considering only one of the two equations of motion in phase space. The corresponding non-interacting system is found to represent Witten's model of SUSY quantum mechanics. Imposing also the second equation of motion the original result of Wigner and Yang is reconsidered by extending their discussion to general symmetric potentials on the real line. As explicit example we discuss the harmonic oscillator and an attractive Coulomb-like potential $V(x) = - \gamma / |x|$. We also establish a Hooke-Newton duality between this Coulomb-like system and the original Wigner-Yang harmonic oscillator system.
papers.authors: Georg Junker

papers.title: Detecting non-Gaussianity and quantum non-Gaussianity via multicopy interference
papers.abstract: We develop tests of non-Gaussianity for bosonic systems based on interference between identically prepared copies of the state. The tests use real orthogonal transformations that mix the copies while preserving their collective mode. These transformations commute with identical Gaussian unitaries applied to each copy, allowing us to derive exact Gaussian benchmarks. For single-mode states, purity alone determines the Gaussian reference value, and any discrepancy certifies non-Gaussianity. A two-copy SWAP measurement supplies the purity calibration, while informative tests within this family begin at three copies. We describe a measurement protocol with finite-sample error bounds that use passive interferometry and photon-number-resolving detectors. We also derive purity-dependent inequalities, including joint constraints on higher-power real moments, whose violation excludes convex mixtures of Gaussian states (thus certifying quantum non-Gaussianity). Finally, we extend the reference formulas to multimode systems and prove completeness of the covariance-calibrated hierarchy for states with finite mean photon number.
papers.authors: Hao Dai, Matteo G. A. Paris, Yue Zhang

papers.title: New gravitational instanton: shadow of an extra dimension
papers.abstract: We present an exact gravitational instanton solution on a five-dimensional, conformally invariant, Kerr-like warped Riemannian brane-world manifold. The geometry can be described as the K\"ahler manifold $\mathbb{C}^1\times\mathbb{C}^1\times \mathbb{R}$. By applying a double cover of $S^3$ through stereographic projection onto $\mathbb{C}P^1\times \mathbb{C}P^1$ of the effective four-dimensional manifold, together with the Klein surface construction, we exploit the underlying $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. The instanton is then obtained by fibering over the antipodal $S^2$. The metric is determined by a first-order differential equation containing an integer parameter, while the equation governing the angular momentum component decouples from the remaining field equations. Finally, we show that our solution admits an analytic complex transformation to a locally conformally related K\"ahler manifold possessing a K\"ahler potential, thereby making the self-dual structure manifest.
papers.authors: Reinoud Jan Slagter

papers.title: A fast dynamo with zero topological entropy
papers.abstract: We construct an autonomous Lipschitz fast dynamo on the flat three-torus whose particle flow has zero topological entropy and whose ideal induction equation has no exponential growth. We perform a multiscale construction starting from the Ponomarenko flow. For every sufficiently small positive magnetic diffusivity, the induction operator on $\mathbb{T}^3$ has an eigenvalue with real part bounded below by a positive constant independent of the diffusivity. A corresponding non-zero real-valued magnetic field satisfies an exact exponential growth law in $\mathrm{L}^2$. For the same velocity field, every solution of the ideal problem grows at most linearly in $\mathrm{L}^2$. Moreover, the particle flow and its inverse have Lipschitz constants growing at most linearly in time and thus zero topological entropy. The velocity field is real-valued, divergence-free, differentiable everywhere and smooth away from one circle, but is not $\mathrm{C}^1$.
papers.authors: Lukas Niebel

papers.title: Load-induced Taylor-Aris dispersion in compliant electroosmotic pumps with viscoelastic electrolytes
papers.abstract: We investigate the dispersion of a passive, neutral solute in a compliant slit, in which electroosmotic flow drives a viscoelastic electrolyte against an outlet pressure load. The electrolyte is modelled using the simplified Phan-Thien-Tanner model with an inviscid Newtonian solvent. Combining lubrication theory, Debye Huckel linearisation and a local elastic-foundation model, we determine the loaded flow and quantify solute dispersion. A central finding is that hydraulic loading fundamentally alters the thin-electric-double-layer limit of shear dispersion. It was observed that shear dispersion vanishes under free-flow conditions, but an adverse pressure gradient continues to support core shear under load, resulting in a finite dispersion plateau even without flow reversal. This plateau increases with hydraulic loading and is further enhanced by viscoelasticity at a fixed throughput fraction. For Newtonian flow, wall expansion leaves the plateau unchanged under constant-current conditions but increases it under constant-voltage conditions. At finite EDL thicknesses, opposing electroosmotic and pressure-driven shear can partially cancel, improving the plate number despite reduced throughput. The combined effects of shear dispersion, molecular diffusion and transit time produce an optimal EDL thickness at prescribed throughput. Joint optimisation shifts the optimum towards free-flow conditions and thinner EDLs for the range of parameters considered. The predicted plate numbers agree closely with Brownian-dynamics simulations for six benchmark cases. These results establish the role of hydraulic loading and wall compliance in controlling the trade-off between pressure delivery and band broadening in compliant electroosmotic pumps.
papers.authors: Subhajyoti Sahoo, Ameeya Kumar Nayak, Kirti Chandra Sahu

papers.title: Diagonally gauged anomaly-free 6D supergravities and their vacua
papers.abstract: We study anomaly-free six-dimensional $N=(1,0)$ supergravities with $n_T=1$ and diagonal $U(1)_{R+}$ or $Sp(1)_{R+}$ gauging. The diagonal group combines R-symmetry with a commuting action on hypermultiplets. We perform bounded searches for anomaly-free models with one or two additional simple gauge group factors of rank at most 30, impose string-charge lattice and positive kinetic term conditions, and tabulate the resulting spectra. The main scans cover $q_{\max}\leq2$ and $d_{\max}\leq3$, where $q_{\max}$ is the largest absolute hyperino charge and $d_{\max}$ the largest diagonal $Sp(1)$ representation dimension, with supplementary searches at larger values. Every hypermultiplet block is required to be nontrivial under at least one additional simple gauge factor. The search has led to a large number of models. Here we give the details of 93 models with $G_+= U(1)_{R+}$ and $q_{\rm max}\le 2$, and 26 models with $G_+=Sp(1)_{R+}$ and $d_{\rm max}\le 3$, and one or two simple group factors. Additional 1341 and 494 models with $G_+=U(1)_{R+}$ with $q_{\rm max}=2$ and $Sp(1)_{R+}$ with $d_{\rm max}=3$, respectively, are posted to the GitHub repository. We establish the existence of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua for all the anomaly free models we have found with $q_{\rm max}=2$ and $d_{\rm max}=3$. We find that such vacua require $q_{\max}>1$ for $U(1)_{R+}$, and $d_{\max}>2$ for $Sp(1)_{R+}$. We also show that every Minkowski vacuum breaks R-symmetry, with the connected unbroken gauge group contained in the additional gauge factors. At two-derivative order, while our anomaly free models do not admit AdS$_6$ solutions, all those with $q_{\rm max} = 2$ and $d_{\rm max}=3$ have non-supersymmetric and unstable dS$_6$ vacua as well.
papers.authors: Xu Guo, Yi Pang, Henning Samtleben, Ergin Sezgin

papers.title: On the effects of emulated quantum layers on CNN performance and explainability for OCT and dementia imaging
papers.abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical convolutional neural networks have been proposed as an alternative to classical deep learning models. However, executing network components on quantum hardware imposes fundamental limitations, such as gradient estimation through repeated measurements, and increasing the number of qubits can lead to trainability problems such as barren plateaus. Moreover, the reported success of these hybrid networks has been linked to quantum architectures that can be efficiently simulated on classical computers. We investigate whether small, classically simulated quantum circuits can serve as useful components within larger models, as a substitute for purely classical layers. We present a systematic comparison between a Hybrid Quantum-inspired CNN (HQiCNN) and standard CNN architectures, where the models differ only in a single intermediate layer: an emulated quantum circuit in the HQiCNN and classical counterparts in the CNN. The models are evaluated on two medical imaging datasets while varying training set size, learning rate, batch size, circuit entanglement and observable se. Under a strict parameter budget, the HQiCNN outperforms the classical baselines. When the classical layer is given more parameters, overall performance becomes comparable, with the HQiCNN showing improvements only in the intermediate-data regime. Removing entanglement yields comparable performance and richer observable sets yield no performance improvement. Finally, we introduce two SHAP-based metrics for comparing model explanations, $|$SHAP$|$IoU and EMD$_{\mathrm{pos}}$. They show that all architectures attend to anatomically plausible regions, and that the spatial attention agreement between them increases with training set size. These results indicate that, under specific data regimes, quantum-inspired hybrid models are a competitive alternative to classical CNNs for medical image classification.
papers.authors: Guillermo Rubi\~nos Rodr\'iguez, Mart\'in Ottavianelli, Mateo Alonso, Gonzalo Bl\'azquez Gil, Boris-Stephan Rauchmann, Pablo D\'iez-Valle, Sergio Altares-L\'opez

papers.title: Static spheres in black hole spacetimes: pairing, energy conditions, and an upper bound on the innermost radius
papers.abstract: Static spheres---spherical surfaces, located outside the event horizon, on which massive test particles can remain at rest with zero angular momentum relative to asymptotic static observers---have recently attracted some attention. In this work, we investigate their existence, relation to the energy conditions, and radial bounds in general static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat black hole spacetimes within general relativity. By analyzing the behavior of a radial function constructed from the mass and radial pressure functions, we prove that, under the weak energy condition (WEC), a static sphere necessarily requires negative radial pressure (tension). Furthermore, for non-extremal black holes satisfying the WEC, we show that any exterior static spheres, if present and non-degenerate, occur in pairs, each consisting of an inner unstable sphere and an outer stable one. Assuming the WEC holds throughout the exterior, the inner static sphere is characterized by a violation of the strong energy condition (SEC), with $\rho+p+2p_T<0$, where $\rho$, $p$, and $p_T$ denote the energy density, radial pressure, and tangential pressure, respectively; the SEC is restored ($\rho+p+2p_T>0$) at the outer sphere; a degenerate static sphere satisfies $\rho+p+2p_T=0$. In addition, focusing on the innermost static sphere and assuming that the WEC holds while the SEC is uniformly violated between the event horizon and this sphere, we derive a rigorous upper bound on its radius. These results establish a direct, analytic link between the energy conditions and the existence of static spheres, and provide a quantitative constraint on the matter environment of black holes possessing such orbits.
papers.authors: Yong Song

papers.title: Continuous Time Quantum Walk Propagation for Irregular Temporal Graph Forecasting
papers.abstract: Continuous time quantum walks built on graph Laplacians produce non monotonic graph propagation features through quantum interference during evolution, which classical diffusion cannot achieve. Such walks deliver a physically motivated propagation scheme for temporal graph signal modeling. We propose Quantum Walk Temporal Architecture (QWTA), which replaces classical graph propagation with a CTQW-type parameterized spectral propagator. QWTA embeds effective observation intervals into the spectral phase modulation of the propagation kernel. QWTA-Base preserves exact CTQW spectral evolution and serves as a physically faithful propagation reference. QWTA-GR further introduces phase soft clipping and gated residual fusion to stabilize propagation. The results show that explicit phase encoding of irregular time intervals, when combined with suitable stabilization, provides a physically motivated and competitive graph propagation design for temporal graph forecasting with missing historical observations.
papers.authors: Jiaqi Sun, Tianhao Li, Zhihao Bian

papers.title: The Norton Theorem for Quantum Circuits and Systems
papers.abstract: It is well known that classical analog circuits and systems benefit from the powerful Thevenin and Norton theorems. These theorems enable rigorous and exact mathematical simplification and representation of the effect of the rest of a system on the part we want to focus on. We show that there are corresponding versions of a "Quantum Norton Theorem" that enable exact simplification and reduction for quantum circuits and systems, not just for one port, but also for multiport and even open quantum systems. We demonstrate the method on two level systems, chains, system environment partitions, Lindblad examples, and Grover search. The Grover examples show how the reduced network isolates the bright pole governing ideal search and exposes how diagonal disorder transfers spectral weight into dark poles that degrade performance. By partitioning finite dimensional Schrodinger dynamics into retained and eliminated sectors, we show that Gaussian elimination gives an exact reduced equation in which the eliminated subsystem appears as a dynamical self energy and a source term. In the circuit representation, these terms become the Norton admittance and Norton current source seen by the retained quantum port. The same Schur complement construction extends to multiport reductions, composite system environment partitions, density matrix dynamics, and Lindblad evolution in Liouville space.
papers.authors: Anthony J. Cressman, Rahul Sarpeshkar

papers.title: SPH methods in the modelling of compact objects
papers.abstract: We review the current status of compact object simulations that are based on the Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method. The first section of this review is dedicated to SPH as a numerical method for Newtonian, ideal gas dynamics and it should be fairly self-contained. It begins with the basics of the method, but also describes recent advances including various meshless derivatives or methods for treating shocks. A separate chapter summarizes general relativistic SPH, including its special relativistic limit, and it explains in some detail the recent development of full numerical relativity in SPH where matter is evolved together with a dynamical spacetime. The remainder of the review has an astrophysical focus, here we discuss the status of the simulations of white dwarf--white dwarf, neutron star--neutron star and neutron star--black hole systems. For each type of system the emphasis is on gravitational-wave-driven mergers, but we also briefly summarize dynamical collisions that can occur in locations with large stellar densities.
papers.authors: Stephan Rosswog

papers.title: Ultraviolet structure of entanglement harvesting from energy density and other quadratic couplings
papers.abstract: We study entanglement harvesting with particle detectors coupled to the renormalized energy density of a massless scalar field. Our analysis identifies the distributional mechanism underlying the persistent ultraviolet divergences previously observed for quadratic detector couplings and shows that the energy density coupling exhibits the same underlying structure. We show that these divergences are controlled by the switching correlation at coincident interaction times and, for smeared detectors, by local derivatives of the spatial overlap. Consequently, pointlike detectors are UV finite whenever the switchings do not overlap. For smooth, rapidly decreasing switchings, they are also UV finite at any fixed nonzero separation. For Gaussian-smeared detectors, the harvesting correlations are automatically finite in 1+1 and 2+1 dimensions, while in higher dimensions the remaining divergences are removed by non-overlapping switchings. Finally, we derive general expressions for arbitrary zero-mean Gaussian Hadamard states and illustrate the formalism with a thermal field state.
papers.authors: Matheus H. Zambianco, Boris Ragula, Eduardo Mart\'in-Mart\'inez

papers.title: Symmetry-based resolution of pseudogauge ambiguities in local equilibrium
papers.abstract: The total angular momentum current can be decomposed into orbital and spin contributions in different ways, known as pseudogauges. This freedom leads to ambiguities in the definition of local-equilibrium density operators, which in turn affect estimates of spin polarization in heavy-ion collisions. In this work, the pseudogauge ambiguity, together with other ambiguities associated with improvements of conserved currents, is reformulated in terms of spurious symmetries corresponding to conserved currents with vanishing total charge. A prescription for the unambiguous definition of a local-equilibrium density operator, defined as deviating from global equilibrium only by small gradients, is introduced using the currents associated with genuine symmetries. The resulting density operator is invariant under transformations that add improvement terms to local currents, including the energy-momentum tensor.
papers.authors: Carlos Hoyos

papers.title: The Status of Single Scalar Field Dark Energy
papers.abstract: We present an assessment of the current observational status of single scalar field models of dark energy. Motivated by recent cosmological measurements -- including baryon acoustic oscillations, Type Ia supernovae, and CMB data -- we examine whether a dynamical scalar field offers a viable explanation for the accelerated expansion of the Universe. Working within an effective field theory (EFT) framework, we argue that cosmological observations are fundamentally limited and can at most constrain a small number of parameters that govern scalar field dynamics. We show that quintessence remains only marginally distinguishable from a cosmological constant, $\Lambda$, and that more general EFT extensions exhibit modest statistical preference, though such evidence is sensitive to data set selection and prior assumptions. These extended models generically predict fifth forces and modifications to the growth of structure, raising challenges from astrophysical constraints. We compare their predictions with current growth rate measurements, Integrated Sachs-Wolfe (ISW) effect and Solar System constraints. We emphasize that viable screening mechanisms remain theoretically non-trivial and observationally testable. On the other hand, we find that current ISW and growth data remain largely in agreement. Looking ahead to Stage IV surveys we forecast improvements in constraints on the dark energy behaviour; although there will be some tightening of bounds, we argue that the problem of underdetermination will persist. We conclude that while single scalar field dark energy remains a natural and flexible framework, its ultimate viability will hinge on improved low-redshift growth measurements and a clearer understanding of gravitational screening.
papers.authors: Carlos Garc\'ia-Garc\'ia, Pedro G. Ferreira, William J. Wolf

papers.title: On perturbations that preserve the connectivity properties in tree percolations
papers.abstract: We consider a general bond percolation on an infinite locally finite tree, where the edge retention probabilities $p_e$ are replaced by $\min\{1,q_{|e|}p_e\}$, where $\{q_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ is a sequence of positive perturbation factors and $|e|$ denotes the distance between the edge $e$ and the root. If the original percolation model admits infinite clusters, it is of interest to investigate under which perturbations $0<q_n\le 1$ this connectivity property is preserved. Conversely, if the original percolation does not admit infinite clusters, we are led to study the stability of such a property under perturbations satisfying $q_n\ge 1$. In both cases, under minimal assumptions on the original model, we show that the percolative behaviour is stable against certain quantitative non-trivial perturbations. We also discuss an application of our results to the Erd\H{o}s similarity conjecture for Cantor sets.
papers.authors: Mirmuhsin Maxmud, Ville Suomala

papers.title: Cosmological implications of $f(T,B)$ gravity: Constraints from recent observations
papers.abstract: In this work, we examine the theoretical framework of modified teleparallel gravity including the boundary term in the action and investigate its cosmological implications for the power-law model $f(T,B)=-T+\alpha(-B)^{\beta}$, aiming to address late-time accelerated expansion and dark energy. Here $T$ denotes the torsion scalar and $B$ represents the boundary term, whose presence allows departures from standard teleparallel dynamics and provides a unified description connecting torsion- and curvature-based formulations, reproducing $f(T)$ and $f(R)$ gravity in appropriate limits. The viability of the model is assessed by confronting its predictions with data and constraining the cosmological and model parameters via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) using cosmic chronometers (CC), the Pantheon plus sample (PPS), and DESI baryon acoustic oscillation Data Release 2 (BAO DR2) datasets, and by comparing its performance with the standard $\Lambda$CDM model. Our results, for the obtained constraints on $\beta$, strongly indicate that, within the adopted parameterization and prior ranges, the data favor a non-zero correction to the boundary term. The AIC shows that the combined CC+PPS dataset mildly favors the $f(T,B)$ model, suggesting an improved fit to late-time observations over $\Lambda$CDM, whereas BIC favors $\Lambda$CDM, since the $f(T,B)$ model is penalized by an extra free parameter from the initial conditions needed to solve the cosmological equations. The model predicts a Hubble constant between the Planck and SH0ES determinations, again consistent with current late-time observations. Background cosmological quantities indicate a dynamical phantom-divide crossing while remaining compatible with observations, yielding a viable expansion history and characteristic dark-energy evolution.
papers.authors: Laxmipriya Pati, Santosh V. Lohakare, S. K. Maurya

papers.title: Fragility of stealth solutions in mimetic gravity
papers.abstract: We study a broad class of constrained mimetic-type extensions of general relativity with action $S=\int{\rm d}^4x\sqrt{-g}\,\bigl(R/2+\lambda\,C[g,\Psi]+{\cal L}_{\rm m}\bigr)$, where $R$ is the Ricci scalar, $\lambda$ is a Lagrange multiplier, $C[g,\Psi]$ is a scalar functional of the metric and generic field content $\Psi$ (possibly involving $\Psi$ and its covariant derivatives) and ${\cal L}_{\rm m}$ is the matter Lagrangian. On the branch $\bar{\lambda}=0$, with the bar denoting a background value, the constrained sector drops out of the background dynamics, so, on domains where a background profile $\bar\Psi$ satisfying $\bar C=0$ exists, the theory admits the corresponding general relativity geometries as stealth solutions. As an explicit illustration, we consider the scalar field case, where $C=g^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\phi\partial_\nu\phi\pm1=0$ becomes a Hamilton-Jacobi equation selecting geodesic congruences. In this setting, we discuss spherically symmetric and rotating stealth profiles using Carter separability. We then analyze perturbations at the general level. The quadratic terms weighted by $\bar\lambda$ vanish on the stealth branch, while the nonlinear constraint still holds order by order and nonlinear interactions need not vanish. Consequently, reproducing GR at the background level does not ensure a uniform $\bar\lambda\to0$ limit for perturbations, and strong coupling may arise.
papers.authors: Alireza Allahyari, Clarisse Donio, Mohammad Ali Gorji, Reera Gorji, Javad T. Firouzjaee

papers.title: Toponium effects on quantum steering and Bell nonlocality of top quarks
papers.abstract: We investigate quantum steering and Bell nonlocality in top-quark pair production at the LHC near threshold. The toponium contribution strengthens the spin-singlet component and substantially enhances the entanglement between the two quark spins. With current LHC data, quantum steering appears to be observable at the $5\sigma$ level provided systematic uncertainties are at 5\% or below. For Bell nonlocality, the statistical significance can also be high close to threshold, but systematics are expected to limit a possible measurement to around $2\sigma$ sensitivity.
papers.authors: J. A. Aguilar-Saavedra, S. Rodr\'iguez-Ben\'itez

papers.title: Gate-Controlled Spin Qubits in Confined Altermagnets
papers.abstract: We propose gate-defined spin qubits in electrostatically confined altermagnetic quantum dots, together with an electrical spin-drive channel that requires neither spin-orbit coupling (SOC) nor micromagnets or field gradients. Elliptical confinement projects the $d$-wave altermagnetic spin splitting onto the discrete dot spectrum, producing a low-energy qubit doublet whose splitting follows the gate geometry, with a microwave-range qubit gap and a meV-range leakage gap over the parameter ranges studied. Because the projected splitting tracks the confinement anisotropy, a phase-controlled resonant quadrupolar gate drive implements $X_{\pi/2}$ and $X_\pi$ rotations in time-dependent simulations. The drive matrix element is set by the non-relativistic altermagnetic hopping rather than by an SOC coefficient, with a static in-plane field of a few tenths of a tesla supplying the transverse mixing. The qubit has no first-order coupling to uniform electric-field noise, and its first-order quadrupolar charge-noise sensitivity vanishes at the circular point, where the drive is strongest. Two-electron configuration-interaction calculations of a double dot yield an isolated logical two-qubit manifold with a nonzero nonlocal Pauli block, and resonant central-barrier modulation implements a perfectly entangling fSim gate. Within this model, confined altermagnets thus provide the ingredients for universal gate-based control from local electrostatic gates; we identify the material and device conditions that a realization must meet.
papers.authors: Hamed Vakili

papers.title: Pauli-Z Moment Matrices in the Variational Quantum Power Method: Goemans-Williamson Rounding, Qubit Locking, and a Correlation-Based Circuit-Cutting Heuristic
papers.abstract: The matrix of single- and two-qubit Pauli-Z expectation values of any quantum state is the moment matrix of its computational-basis outcome distribution; it therefore lies in the cut polytope and, in particular, is a feasible point of the degree-2 Sum-of-Squares (Goemans-Williamson, GW) relaxation. Applying GW random-hyperplane rounding to this matrix yields cuts of expected weight at least alpha_GW times the state's energy. This observation and the resulting bound are not new: the bound is the GW inequality applied to the circuit's covariance matrix, and it was stated and used in exactly this form by Martinez, Fawzi and Stilck Franca, who interpret it as showing that a classical surrogate nearly reproduces the circuit and add noisy-circuit guarantees and hardware experiments; relax-and-round of QAOA correlation matrices, with spectral rather than hyperplane rounding, was introduced earlier by Dupont and Sundar. The bound is also not stronger than what direct computational-basis sampling of the state already gives in expectation. In this note we revisit the bound as a post-processing of the two-point data produced by variational algorithms such as QAOA and the Variational Quantum Power Method (VQPM), and give an energy-leakage bound for VQPM qubit locking. We further discuss a heuristic that uses the connected Z-correlation matrix to propose candidate qubit bipartitions for circuit cutting, in the spirit of existing correlation- and mutual-information-based partitioning methods, together with product-state error bounds in terms of quantum mutual information. Pairwise Z-correlations neither certify product structure of the state nor factorization of the underlying unitary, and the error bounds require quantities not available from Z-data alone.
papers.authors: Ammar Daskin

papers.title: Gas-induced gravitational-wave dephasing and accretion periodicities of live post-Newtonian massive black hole binaries: warm disk
papers.abstract: We perform 3D hydrodynamical simulations of an equal-mass quasi-circular live $10^6 {\rm M}_\odot$ massive black hole binary (MBHB) embedded in a prograde, locally isothermal circumbinary disk (CBD) with 0.1 aspect ratio. The binary evolves under the effect of gaseous torques and 2.5 post-Newtonian dynamics. We follow the gravitational-wave (GW) driven inspiral from 53 Schwarzschild radii ($r_s$) down to merger, over 1.5 years. Comparing the GW inspiral rate with the viscous inflow, we find the binary to decouple from the CBD just $\approx 2$ days before merger. We measure gas torques (gravitational and accretion) with and without concurrent GW emission, finding that their sums agree to within $\lesssim 5\%$ down to $25 r_s$. We then measure a gas-induced GW phase shift that peaks at $\approx 5\times10^{-4}$ rad near $45 r_s$, as the gas torque slows the inspiral, and then changes sign as the accreted mass accelerates it. It is LISA-detectable only at $z\lesssim 0.1$. We further characterize the mass accretion rate modulations. All three fundamental periodicities, associated with the "lump" at the inner cavity edge, the binary orbital period, and half of it, are shifted to lower frequencies by precession. We measure the shift at the orbital period, due to relativistic apsidal precession, in an inspiraling binary for the first time, and newly identify the other two as due to the precession of the eccentric cavity. Our results have implications for multi-messenger astronomy, since observation of accretion rate modulation by LSST/Roman surveys and phase-shift by LISA will provide crucial information on the complex environment surrounding MBHBs.
papers.authors: Mudit Garg, Alessia Franchini, Alessandro Lupi

papers.title: Quantum mechanics in configuration space in context
papers.abstract: The formalism of quantum mechanics in configuration space (QMCS) [Bukhari et al., New J. Phys. 27, 084501 (2025)] has been introduced to unify the modelling of photons and quantum mechanical particles. In this paper, we illustrate that QMCS also increases the continuity between quantum and classical mechanics, since it can be used to obtain both their predictions. Being based on a physically motivated quantisation of Newtonian mechanics, QMCS makes a clear distinction between the velocity observable v and the generator for spatial translations, i.e. the momentum operator p, of mechanical particles. In contrast, standard quantum mechanics, which is based on Hamiltonian mechanics, relates velocity directly to momentum rather than treating them as independent observables. Despite having many formal similarities with Hilbert space formulations of classical mechanics, QMCS is a quantum theory. To illustrate this and to further explore the relations between QMCS and alternative approaches, this paper studies quantum mechanical particles moving in free space as an example.
